rows.text: Memories... Broken...
rows.speaker: Sound of Oronyx

rows.text: Mother... Where...
rows.speaker: Sound of Oronyx

rows.text: Mother... Who are they calling out for?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Oh right, there's something that I have to tell you. The Chrysos Heirs already know everything that has happened to you...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I was too worried, so I told them everything... Ugh, please don't hate me, okay?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: It's just as I suspected. The troubles afflicting the Flame-Chase Journey aren't just external issues. The complex internal politics and interpersonal relationships are also exacerbating the problem.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: We can't let our guard down yet... We have to find out where we stand in this large interwoven web.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's almost time for the ritual. Get some rest, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Get some rest and wait for the trial.
Wait, I still have some things to do.
There are still things that you need to attend to? Alright, but don't overexert yourself. Make sure to keep yourself well rested.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Accepting a Titan's trial is a very peculiar experience... I'm afraid that I'm not able to accurately describe it. You can only go and experience it for yourself.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I believe that you'll be able to pull it off.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I can still vividly recall when you entered the Vortex of Genesis for the first time. At that time, I could never have imagined that a guest from beyond the sky would shoulder the fate of Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Don't feel burdened. Just like during the trial of Strife, Trinnon and Phainon will be waiting for you outside. If something unforeseen were to occur, they will intervene in the trial and rescue you.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: May {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} bless you.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer]... I'm sorry but I'm not sure what I should say to help calm your nerves.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Right, perhaps something like: As long as you can successfully complete this trial, the rest of the Flame-Chase Journey will be smooth-sailing?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: No, that sounds a little strange... Don't worry, it won't take up too much of your time? Um... Don't worry, you'll definitely make it back alive?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Sorry, it seems like I've made the mood even heavier. In any case... May everything go your way.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Let's do that then, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You notice the resolute yet gentle look in Dan Heng's eyes. He doesn't want to burden you with his worries in words. You already understand — his trust in you transcends words. As he once said, "It's not the time for sorrow yet."
Next, he will go to the Grove to check out the situation, while you should be looking for Castorice with Mem.
[Trailblazer], and Mem, thank you.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Your resolves cannot be questioned. We praise your pure selflessness and courage... May {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} light your path forward.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Get ready to assume {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s divinity, Trailblazer.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Mmm, it seems that this sacred beast is just as indispensable, given their intricate ties to the Titan.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I understand. It was the sacred beast's idea, after all. However, it warrants careful consideration, given their intricate ties to the Titan.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Hehe, thanks to you, I've evolved from a little dog into a sacred beast!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: On the contrary, you are the only one who qualifies to attain divinity. Yet, for that very reason, I do not wish to pressure you.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: It's exceedingly rare to find a capable Chrysos Heir. If this path proves unattainable, I am willing to lower my expectations.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: It's exceedingly rare to find a capable Chrysos Heir. If this path proves unattainable, I am willing to lower my expectations.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: There are still many priests of Janusopolis and their descendants in the city. If I'm left with no other option, I'll try to find someone worthy among them.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Exactly! We can't have the civilians bear the risks, can we?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Don't worry! With me by your side, even if things go south, you'll be heading straight to heaven!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Don't give up now, [Trailblazer]!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: We've come so far, and everyone is counting on you to be the hero!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Since you've made your decision, go back to the bath chamber and get some rest. Trinnon will call for you when the ceremony is ready.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Please, trust me on this. At the very least... can you speak with them in person?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I... It's nothing. I only came to discuss some matters with Lady Aglaea.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It just contains an allegory: In a faraway land, in a city known as Styxia, a dragon corrupted by the black tide descended one day, swooping upon the city like Death itself.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: No, it's just an ordinary book. It's definitely not some kind of unique copy.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It mustn't have been easy for Cas to narrate this story so calmly...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Huh? How... How was it touching...?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: The author of this book is Archepia, a wandering bard who traveled to many cities.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That's right... Writing, drawing, and taking photographs... It seems like human nature to try and leave records of things.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Good news? I wouldn't call it that.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I wouldn't call it trouble. I just think it will be favorable if the both of you understand the situation in Okhema better.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Do you remember the Council of Elders that was on our heels previously? It seems like they've made their move.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Despite her vision and wisdom that spans across thousands of years, even she cannot win over the hearts of everyone.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Perhaps you should retake some exams next time we visit Paperfold University.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Every five to ten years, the Council of Elders organizes a citizens' assembly at Dawncloud.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: No. Although we might be mentioned, the Council of Elders has another target in mind.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Me?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: It looks like you've realized it as well.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I'm afraid that the Council of Elders might want to take advantage of Professor Anaxa.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Allow me to apologize for the fact that we always seem to be troubling you. I hope that {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} will show more benevolence and be more accommodating. I remember that they seemed quite fond of you back in the Abyss.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: This is just an exaggerated figure of speech to express how nervous I'm feeling right now!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Let's just hope that everything goes well. After all, as someone who has earned the gaze of an Aeon, you should be able to overcome the trial of a regional god just fine.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Speaking of which, I don't recall seeing any rubber duck toys in the baths of Okhema. It seems like they only have these... seals?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There are still things that you need to attend to? Alright, but don't overexert yourself. Make sure to keep yourself well rested.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That's right! Look, look! I don't know what happened, but I'm able to talk! Testing, testing, one, two, three. Testing, Testing one, two, three...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Right? I think that it's amazing, too! Testing, testing, one, two, three. Testing, testing, one, two, three...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I have such a cute voice! It must be because of all the memories that I collected. They allowed me to grow beyond expectations!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: There's something that... I've never told you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...For you to be able to say that even now... You're truly impressive.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I'm not sure whether the gaze of Fuli has anything to do with this matter, but according to the Titan, you are living in the form of a memory right now, just like those objects of the past in the miracles of Oronyx.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...That's beside the point.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's not time for us to despair yet. There must be a way to save you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: For a while, I also thought that the Stellaron was your life support system, but it seems like... this hypothesis has been disproven.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I'm sorry, I just wanted to verify once again...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Back at the Grove, I was puzzled as to why you were not affected by my curse. I thought that it might have been the special ability of a traveler from beyond the sky. Never did I expect that this would be the true reason...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Please pardon me.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I have never touched the living in this way before. If my actions are in any way disrespectful, I hope that you can forgive me...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...My apologies, I will stop making such unreasonable requests.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I... seem to have caught a glimpse of something. Your soul is currently roaming someplace and cannot find a way to escape...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Castorice once again places her palm on your face. Her shivers calm somewhat this time.

Lady Aglaea and Lord Phainon are currently discussing some matters in the baths. They're worried about you, too. If possible, please go there and let them know that you're well. Although I don't actually know whether your current situation can be described as "well"...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I beg you, please forgive me!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: That's the medical prowess of the Twilight Courtyard. Amazing, isn't it?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Well, at least you look no different from the living. I think that most living people don't even look as good as you do.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You've completed the trial of Time, and I have to admit that the process went better than I expected. Even in the end, that Titan's heart still showed a soft spot for humankind.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: It is my duty. We too require you to bear the divine position of Time.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Don't take it to heart, [Trailblazer]. After all, you've already created countless miracles along the way, right?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: But before that, just...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: The last time I heard this, things didn't turn out that well.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: That doesn't seem appropriate for the current mood, so let's just leave the farewells for next time.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Sound of Oronyx

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Something... important...?
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: You have... potential... strength...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Future...?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Time... never compromises... never bears grudges...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: (Tribios' memory has unveiled the very first prophecy...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ("All shall bid farewell to one, {RUBY_B#Only one shall live till the end, and they alone will witness Era Nova}and that person alone will witness the miracle.{RUBY_E#} Such is the will of fate.")
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (If I take on {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx's{RUBY_E#} trial, will the prophecy come to pass for me as well?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Regardless, I must give Aglaea an answer...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Some time ago.
Ah, it's you, Cas. I finished the anthology of poems you lent me — here it is.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I thought you'd be too preoccupied to find time for reading.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Precisely because of these obligations, I felt compelled to read it swiftly.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Wouldn't all these preoccupations slow your pace?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: On the contrary. Knowing that time is limited can push one to overcome their limitations. The weight of these responsibilities seems to have enhanced my reading efficiency.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I understand completely. During my time at the Grove, the closer exams drew, the more efficient I became at tackling everyday mundane tasks — anything but my actual studies.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Precisely.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: As I remember, you and Phainon were both disciples of the Nousporists. I assume that Anaxa's exams were as unreasonable as the man himself, correct?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: The courses Professor Anaxa taught were... Introduction to Alchemy and History of Mythology. To be perfectly honest, those two courses were the students' greatest nightmares.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The history of mythology, taught by the blasphemous "Great Performer" himself... I can imagine their fear.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Now that I think about it, students would often rush to the podium during class to challenge him on those blasphemous ideas.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: May I ask, Lady Aglaea, has your relationship with Professor Anaxa always been like this?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: He openly dismisses people's faith, and questions the very justification of the Flame-Chase Journey. Our positions have been destined to be at odds. While you were studying there, I assume you must have heard of his nickname.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ..."a dromas draped in finery"?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: As I see it, this nickname is more of an insult to the dromas.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Hehe...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Despite his insufferable arrogance, I do hold a certain respect for his nature as a scholar. To remain true to his principles, he is unafraid to stand opposed to the world — and that requires considerable resolve.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Anaxagoras' life is almost like a satire: as a Chrysos Heir, he refuses to heed the prophecy, while he disrespects the gods...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...The gods have chosen him.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: He was indeed chosen by {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Is something weighing on you, Cas? The golden thread is quivering. I sense there's more to this exchange than idle chatter.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: With all due respect, I'd like to know what you plan to do with him.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: In light of his assistance in the battle against the Flame Reaver, I am willing to grant him some time to find a way to remove the Coreflame.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: However, if Anaxa decides to make any move that places us in danger, I will not hesitate to take extreme measures.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Just as I feared...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The Flame-Chase Journey is the destined path for the Chrysos Heirs, yet he now seems more like an empty shell. Given his strong sense of self-respect, I trust that Anaxagoras will make the right decision.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Still, I can't help but hope for another possibility...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Perhaps Anaxa will also overcome his limitations, now that he knows time is limited.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I understand your stance. Let's continue this discussion another time.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: But now, let's greet our guest.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: You're here, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Does this mean you're ready to take on {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s trial?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Surrendering the Coreflame is a Chrysos Heir's duty. Your selfless assistance is deeply appreciated.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: However, I urge you to carefully consider the risks of accepting the trial: Becoming a demigod means forsaking your humanity. You will inherit Oronyx's divinity and bear the Time of Amphoreus, all on your own.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: From that point onward, your fate will be forever intertwined with ours, never to be separated again — until the end of Genesis.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: As for the trial, you have nothing to fear... The Time Titan may be willful at times, but they never caused us any harm.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Myth has it that {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} opposes mortals, but to me, they just seem a bit timid... like a child.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: It looks like you know that Titan rather well.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Oddly enough, I don't remember ever meeting them, but the moment I saw [Trailblazer], {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s memories were already in my head.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...Memories that exist outside of your own experiences?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I can't explain why, but I can vouch for Mem's words. When I was in the Abyss, I heard the Titan's groans — full of pain and grievances, yet without any ill will.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I get the feeling that if we don't meet {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}, we'll be missing out on something huge!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: It is difficult for me as the guide to absolve myself from blame for things to have progressed to this point. Time and again, you have risen to the occasion for Okhema. Merely rewarding you with some Honeydew is no longer able to express the extent of our gratitude.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: When the dust settles, I hope that we'll have the chance to have a long chat regarding your return journey and the curse of the sky... It's about time that we lift the taboo and discuss things openly.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: A few days later at the Vortex of Genesis...
[Trailblazer], the {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s vacant totem awaits.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: If you have already made your preparations to become a pillar of Amphoreus, please step forward.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Sound of Oronyx

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Sound of Oronyx

rows.text: *slap*... *slap*...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Wake up... [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: How is it? How do you feel?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Also, listen... The words of the Titan are becoming clearer.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Mother... Mother...
rows.speaker: Sound of Oronyx

rows.text: It hurts... Have I finally reached the end? Are the years of isolation... coming to an end?
rows.speaker: Sound of Oronyx

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}... How heartbreaking. Ever since the figure draped in the black cloak robbed them of their Coreflame, they have been relegated to waiting in isolation in such a confined space...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: We are going to help alleviate their pain, right?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer], I'm right here.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You hear soft steps coming closer, one step at a time...
Please stay there and slowly turn around...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: For some reason, you feel you have seen this scene before.
You want to turn your head, but you glimpse a dash of purple brushing past your face. Then...
A chill seeps through your skin, spreading into your veins. Thump... thump... your heartbeat begins to slow.
I'm sorry. I should have noticed that something was amiss earlier...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Aside from your vision, your senses grow more acute. You feel the presence of a purple sea...
And then, and then...
Your vision blurs, and cold reality fades into a purple ocean...
In the blink of an eye, time seems to have frozen beneath that cold sensation, and you just happened to close your eyes...
A subtle fragrance of an unnamed flower fills your senses, its sweetness making you forget the need to breathe.
You realize you are still alive — no, to be more precise... your death was not thorough.

The coldness of the initial touch dispersed as quickly as it came, and replacing it... was the touch of fingertips, and a tremble born of trepidation that originated from a certain lanky arm. Her quivering finger gently brushed against your cheek, causing a faint tickle.
Just as I expected... I cannot feel anything...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer], if my abrupt behavior just now offended you, I hope that you can forgive me.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I'm just thinking... If your soul has really left your body, as a mortician, I might be able to trace where it has gone to.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Cas, did you find anything?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: My apologies, not as of yet... Perhaps I have overestimated my capabilities.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But... {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer], would you be willing to let me try again? This time, I'll increase the area of contact slightly. Perhaps the result might be different this time...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But perhaps... it might not be a bad thing. If your soul is still wandering around, it means that we still have time... We have a chance to find it before the fingers of {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} sweep everything away.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Clues... Just a few more. I need more guidance...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Huh.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The connection has been severed. With my strength... I'm not able to trace it.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Ahh, don't mind {M#him...}{F#her...} [Trailblazer] is just feeling a little nervous and thinks that... Right, {M#he}{F#she} thinks that things are moving a little too quickly!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: It was me, I was a little too hasty. Don't worry, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer]. Although we currently have no leads, I will do my best to search for the whereabouts of {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}, bring back their Coreflame, and personally return to you... the life that you have lost too soon.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I... know that I'm lacking in confidence, but I hope that you can keep this promise of mine in mind. Before I manage to deliver on this promise... please do your best to hang on.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Amphoreus... needs you.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Also, please accept this Styxian fable... Reading can help one to focus and relax... I hope that reading this can help tide you through this difficult period.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...They're here.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: [Trailblazer]! Hyacine said that you'd definitely wake up. How... do you feel?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: However, I never expected that... two people who have cheated death would appear in Okhema at the same time.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: That's what we have been talking about. Ugh, Mydei has been in Okhema for such a long time but — has no one ever thought to study his indestructible body? If there were even any minor breakthroughs, we wouldn't be as clueless as we are right now...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Many have had this idea, but so far, there have been no results. If it were successful, {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} wouldn't have disappeared without a trace.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Nevertheless, now is not the time for us to give up. At the very least, we can still see a glimmer of hope.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Cipher... If anyone in this world knows the whereabouts of Death, it would be her.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I'll try and get her to return to Okhema but do be prepared for a less-than-ideal outcome. Please understand that throughout the history of Amphoreus, no one has ever managed to escape the clutches of Death. At the end of time, Thanatos silently awaits all.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: What's wrong, Aglaea?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Omens always come in pairs. A tiny air current will eventually brew into a storm that tears the sky apart.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: It's Anaxagoras. He has initiated contact with the Council of Elders.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: In the end, it has still come down to this...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I earnestly hope that your assessment of him is accurate, Phainon.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Otherwise, the efforts of my teacher and I over the past millennium... might be reduced to dust because of that "Great Performer."
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Sound of Oronyx

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}... Their soul has been waiting for a long time.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Perhaps they're also quietly waiting for the arrival of their successor.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Don't worry, Aglaea. [Trailblazer] is tougher than I am, right?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Don't worry, [Trailblazer]. You're tougher than I am, right?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Let's go, [Trailblazer]!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Traveler from beyond the sky, let us pray that the Titan acknowledges your worthiness.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Although [Trailblazer] loves cracking jokes at inopportune times, {M#his}{F#her} determination is as strong as the Chrysos Heirs. {M#He}{F#She} will definitely succeed.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: While {F#she's}{M#he's} away... I would like to have a chat with you, Aglaea.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Speak, I'm listening.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: You... It's you... I remember you.
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Sky father... has gazed upon you...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Mother... is calling for you...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: The Titan's words are indistinct. Each syllable emerging from the mist seem to be cloaked in frost — symbolizing memory.
Sky father... has chosen you...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: A majestic voice pierces through the golden mist, reaching the unseen mountain walls in the distance, reflecting, and returning to your ears as an echo. Within the echo, you seemingly could make out... the cry of a baby.
Mother... is no longer responding...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: An important... matter...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}, listen to me...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Aren't you tired? Throughout the long years, you have always been protecting the fate of Amphoreus. Each time people draw strength from within their memories, every single ripple falls onto your shoulders.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: There's no need for you to bear this any longer, {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}. From today onwards, someone else will bear Time on your behalf. This is why we have come.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...Freedom... Freedom?
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: I want... freedom...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Oh, poor child, everything will be fine. Let us help you... You can have a good rest now.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Willpower... powerful... and tenacious...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: But... you lack... something...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Just... one thing...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Lacking something... What is it?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: What you lack...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Is... a future...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Traveler from the sky... You should have... dissipated already...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: The gaze from sky father... stabilized... your form...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Because... from the moment you crossed the sky... your life was cast away...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Right now, you... are simply a collection of walking memories...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: What... H—How is that possible!?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: The space... is collapsing...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Someone must... inherit... the authority of Time...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: If the pillar is lost... the laws of Time... will collapse...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Amphoreus... will succumb to... eternal disorder...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Never forgives... never makes a choice...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Child of humanity... Titans... Mother... Sky father...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Time... restrains everything that exists in this world...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s divinity... is dissipating? Is the trial coming to an end?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Pathstrider of Remembrance... my strength... I shall entrust it to you...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: The fate of the world... if you wish to... save it...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Go and find... your future that has been stolen...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Even if that means... you'll have to cheat death...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: You'll have to challenge that... {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Hand of Shadow{RUBY_E#} clasped with unyielding fingers...
rows.speaker: Oronyx

rows.text: Before the passing of fifteen {RUBY_B#Dawn}Entry Hours{RUBY_E#}... Go forth and reclaim your future...
This is the true trial of "time"...
I didn't expect you to agree to Lady Caenis' invitation... What a wonderful turn of events.
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: To tell you the truth, there are many people who hold grudges against that Lady Goldweaver...
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: You truly are a strict teacher.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Of course. This is how I've always been.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I was fortunate enough to have the opportunity to discuss a treatise about the Venerationists with your teacher, Empedocles.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Yet, it seems you subscribe to the Nousporists instead, Lord Anaxa? I've heard that this school of thought is one with many detractors.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: It's normal for ideas to have supporters and dissenters, just like how there are two types of people in this world — geniuses and dimwits.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: A bygone myth tells of an occasion where {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} once answered their followers' questions on the peak of the holy mountain.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Their followers have since believed that scaling this Titan cliff is one way of being with the god.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Hear that? It's not every day that you get to climb a mountain with {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}. You should sing me a hymn of praise.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: ...Titan hymns are beyond me.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: (This is a... departed spirit...?)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I'm fine...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: If this is indeed as I thought... then this will be very amusing.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: They're gone?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: (Hmph. Doesn't matter... I can do this myself.)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: (Looks like I'm nearly there now... The land of the dead.)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Sorry to keep you waiting, Lord Anaxagoras.
She's been waiting. Follow me, please.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Professor Anaxa...
rows.speaker: Young Scribe

rows.text: Over here...
rows.speaker: Young Scribe

rows.text: Hmph, even blasphemous scholars can come here, it seems?
rows.speaker: Wizened Priest

rows.text: Looks like my presence here is quite unwelcome.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh my! Could it be that the Great Tree painted in this mural... is actually depicting me?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Welcome to the Demigod Council, esteemed guests.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Hah, you two again...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: So, we meet again... I'm sure you wouldn't mind a snooping ear?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: "O beautiful old world, where are you now?"
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: "O legendary Era Chrysea, return to the mortal realm!"
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: "Splendid gods once walked the paths we walk."
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: "Alas, all that's left of that warmth is a hazy mirage."
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: ...Why are you chanting that too?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Lord Lygus and Lady Caenis are just ahead.
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: I'll take my leave for now.
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: Isn't that the "dromas draped in finery"?
rows.speaker: Mocking Scholar

rows.text: ...Avoid his gaze. I don't acquaint myself with blasphemers.
rows.speaker: Pious Scholar

rows.text: Don't worry, he's too full of pride to pay us any attention.
rows.speaker: Mocking Scholar

rows.text: Your nickname is "dromas" as well? You must really like those creatures.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: A student of Empedocles? I hear that his views run counter to the Venerationists.
rows.speaker: Stern Councilor

rows.text: This is what being a scholar is about: A collision of ideas only occurs when there are differences in beliefs, and it is such collisions that lead to progress.
rows.speaker: Amiable Councilor

rows.text: Yet in my view, there are only right and wrong perspectives, neither of which can coexist with the other.
rows.speaker: Stern Councilor

rows.text: What radical thinking... I guess this is why the children of humanity always squabble with each other.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: How boring.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You seem to be avoiding that "Goldweaver" person. Why don't you address her face to face?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I have nothing to talk about with her... Since you're in my brain, you can look for the reason yourself.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh... The leader of the Flame-Chase Journey and a demigod of Mnestia...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: You're really searching through my brain? What are you treating it as, some sort of toy?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Regardless, you think quite highly of her, no?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: That's because I'm a teacher who grades everyone fairly.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: If you need to organize your thoughts, please go ahead. But please don't go too far away, lest... complications arise.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: If you need to organize your thoughts, please go ahead. But please don't go too far away, lest... complications arise.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: I believe you're aware of Castorice the executioner. Long before I returned to Okhema, Aglaea had already dispatched her to monitor me. If I weren't able to reach this place in time, I would have been forced to meet {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} first.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: If Aglaea required a suitably intelligent Chrysos Heir, then I'm the best fit for her needs. However, it's quite evident that she has no need for a Chrysos Heir who could break free of her control at any time.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hah... I understand what you mean.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Although the circumstances are rather unfortunate, from an objective point of view, it is an undeniable fact that ever since the Grove was attacked, I have become the de facto leader of the Grove.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Aglaea's authoritarianism, conceit, and arrogance have granted her unfettered control for the most part. Yet, these traits are also her greatest weakness. If I can render her helpless by forcing her to experience the agonizing pain of betrayal, I am certain she will never recover from such a setback.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: In the name of {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}, Okhema thanks you for your sincere and valuable thoughts.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Hmph, surely you jest. My loyalty does not need to be proven. The fact that the Council of Elders is asking for proof of my loyalty is itself akin to a form of betrayal.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Huh...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Not long ago...
Hehe...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I'm back here again.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I remember this dream. This realm is covered in a silk-like fog, and the land is barren and harsh. The crowd of travelers leaves tracks everywhere.
Hey! Excuse me — what is this place? Where in Amphoreus are we?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The mutters of the traveler are in a language I'm unable to comprehend. Or perhaps, they're just distracted and ignored my question.
Tell me, which Titan reigns over this land and how do I find them?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Hand of... Shadow...{RUBY_E#}
rows.speaker: Wandering Traveler

rows.text: Hand of Shadow, Thanatos?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hmm, could this... possibly be the nether realm?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Not... nether realm...
rows.speaker: Wandering Traveler

rows.text: Then where is this? River of Souls? The outskirts of the nether realm? Are you heading downstream toward the nether realm?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The nether realm... Nothing but an illusion...
rows.speaker: Wandering Traveler

rows.text: Titan... Rejects... You... Me...
rows.speaker: Wandering Traveler

rows.text: Listen...
rows.speaker: Wandering Traveler

rows.text: What?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The traveler lifts their wrinkled fingers and remains silent.
I look in the direction they are pointing and listen closely. There, a massive shadow brought the sound of rushing tides.
The sound of tides...?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I can hear it.
I hear it, deep within the tides, beyond the closed gates of {RUBY_B#nether realm}the void world{RUBY_E#}...
A voice about to recount something.
Child of humanity...
...is it death's embrace you yearn for with such urgency?
Oh, you have awoken. Welcome back to the mortal realm.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Your consciousness is dissipating much faster than I expected... Ultimately, it seems like the Titan's Coreflame is incompatible with a mortal body.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: How much longer can my consciousness remain in the mortal realm?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: In my estimation, at best, you'll see fifteen more {RUBY_B#dawn}Entry Hours{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Heh, fifteen days and nights...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What is it? Are you finally starting to become attached to the mortal world now?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: On the contrary, fifteen days feel a little too long for solving a singular problem.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hehe...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Stop giggling. It's time for us to go. The messenger from the Council of Elders is almost here.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Let me ask you one more question. Are you really planning to betray Aglaea's will?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: What betrayal is there to speak of when I was never loyal to her to begin with?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What about that white-haired student of yours? Acting so recklessly... Do you not care about what might happen to him?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: There will be a price to pay for blind faith. This is also a lesson for Phainon.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: It's been a while, Lord Anaxagoras.
I greet you on behalf of all the citizens of Okhema and express my deepest regret about what happened at the Grove of Epiphany.
It's you? I never expected that you would personally come and meet me.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: By {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} and {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#} above, I have come as a testament to the justice of the Council of Elders.
There are Antikytherans here? They have been a rare sight ever since the Chrysos War.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I extend to you my utmost respect, revered Titan.

I am Lycurgus, though you may call me Lygus. Holding an honorary position within the Council of Elders in Okhema, and as the Theoros, I stand to protect the right of all upright citizens to express themselves freely.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Heh... You can see them, too?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You know about us. We Antikytherans perceive the world through the amplitude and frequency of souls...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: ...Just as I am conscious that Lady Aglaea is secretly listening in on our private meeting from afar. If necessary, Lord Anaxagoras, I can sever the golden thread to protect your fundamental rights.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: The demigod should know better, for such is her station. Spare those poor threads, and just let her listen to my words. They shall serve only to unveil her own folly.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: May I interpret this as you having a countermeasure?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I need not any plan, because she can do nothing other than petty espionage. As the citizens' assembly approaches and with {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s fall, any attempt to capture the Coreflame within me will only usher chaos and calamity — a truth she undoubtedly comprehends.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: While I, Anaxagoras, serving as the Grove's special envoy to Okhema's citizens' assembly, have long known the extent of your abilities...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Let's forego the formality of asserting authority, Lord Lygus. Lead the way.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Very well. Surely Lady Caenis would appreciate such assertiveness in an ally.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Is there something on your mind, Lord Anaxagoras?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Nothing really. It's just a question that I contemplate every time before I ascend Dawncloud: For the Titans, does the falling equate to death?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: A pondering truly deep. Time is on our side. Do you mind sharing your reflections with me?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: While all living beings must ultimately face their demise, {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} has yet to meet theirs. Their journey continues unhurriedly along this long path.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Are you suggesting that {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} may not have truly passed?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Yes, for dying implies an ongoing process, an action, whereas death signifies a static state, a definitive termination.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: In contrast to mortals, Titans exist on a grander scale of space and time, thus elongating their passage into death. The notion of their "fall" is but a misinterpretation born of mortal ignorance.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: An intriguing concept, albeit challenging to substantiate. After all, {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} has maintained a profound silence ever since the Era Erasa, while scholars and priests alike have conveyed the message of the gods' imminent fall.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Perhaps the gods, in their arrogance, deemed it beneath them to reveal their perspectives to mortals.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Could you elaborate on your statement?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}, the kin of the sky father as recounted in myths, now resides within my brain. Were I to inquire, {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} would have no cause to refuse.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: That very well could be true, but what if the Worldbearing Titan still chooses to remain silent?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Heh, in that case, the myths crafted by the people of Amphoreus are nothing more than pitiful jests.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: It's worth a try, I believe, and I'd love to witness the fruits of your theory and the change it may bring to this imperiled world.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Because I completely concur with you on this aspect: If the Titan has indeed met their end, any response from them would be impossible...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Heh... The children of humanity have indeed created a spectacle.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Welcome to Dawncloud. The atmosphere here carries a greater sense of solemnity than the mundane clamor of the Marmoreal Palace, with entry permitted only to the invited.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Only esteemed beings grace this place, and among them, I've received priests, scholars, warriors... And now, we even have the honor to be in the presence of a Titan. What a joyous occasion!
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Hmph... Once deemed a blasphemer, now a surrogate for revered divinity. The honor should rightfully be mine, shouldn't it?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I'll notify Caenis and the others of your arrival. Kindly wait for a moment. A soldier will be here to guide you shortly.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: In the meanwhile, you are welcome to explore the vicinity, but kindly remain within the guards' view. Delaying the crucial meeting is something none of us wish to see, I presume.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I'm well aware of Caenis' methods. There's no need to emphasize that.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: As you wish. Your cooperation is much appreciated.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Alas... I had hoped for a brilliant plan from you, but it turns out you just left one cage to enter another.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Save your concerns. I know very well what I'm doing.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hehe, I shall depart to explore the surroundings, then.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Now that I look around... I wonder if there are any murals bearing my portrait around here. I'm quite intrigued to see how the children of humanity beyond the Grove perceive another Titan.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Off you go. I won't be joining you.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: (This Titan appears to be quite at ease... I should investigate the Council of Elders' recent activities first.)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Be aware, I can hear you perfectly well from here.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Tsk...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Professor Anaxa? Word has it that the scholars of the Grove valiantly perished resisting the black tide. To find you here safe and sound... Thank the fates!
rows.speaker: Young Scribe

rows.text: You could say it's the fates toying with us.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Haha, it's only the Kremnoans and Aidonians who chase glory through death. But your survival is a victory in itself! I'd settle for that gladly!
rows.speaker: Young Scribe

rows.text: So, are you here to report the incident to the Council? I heard that after the black tide devoured the Grove, Okhema would be next in line. Even with the demigod of Strife standing alongside humankind...
rows.speaker: Young Scribe

rows.text: Tell me, how much does the Council of Elders know about the black tide?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Once Caenis and her followers learned of {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} and {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx's{RUBY_E#} fall, they proclaimed in the Council that the Flame-Chasers could no longer stand against the calamity alone...
rows.speaker: Young Scribe

rows.text: Yet, when {RUBY_B#Mydei}the crown prince{RUBY_E#} ascended to godhood and repelled the black tide, she immediately altered her tune, declaring that all was resolved beyond Okhema, with the only remaining menace now being Aglaea and her adherents. They might well make their move at the upcoming citizens' assembly.
rows.speaker: Young Scribe

rows.text: No surprises there, those shifty opportunists... Thank you for your honesty, virtuous student.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hehe, being an opportunist could very well be a facet of wisdom...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Shouldn't you be searching for murals of yourself? I've had enough of your prattling.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I was really curious to see how you would find the middle ground between both factions, so I came to listen in.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: But it seems as though this Caenis is much more ruthless than Aglaea... If so, why do you want to work with her? Could it be that perhaps you've decided to readily surrender this hollow shell of yours just because you feel like death is fast approaching?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hmph, I'm afraid you'll be sorely disappointed if that's what you truly think.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hah, Anaxagoras? I thought that you had died to the black tide, just like the other scholars.
rows.speaker: Wizened Priest

rows.text: As Kephale's priest, are you not aware of the decorum of respecting the dead?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Surely you jest! You blasphemous heretics are not worthy of respect from the supreme being.
rows.speaker: Wizened Priest

rows.text: Let me remind you that you're currently in Dawncloud, so you had better keep your deranged language to yourself. I am no longer that altar servant from years ago who could only acquiesce to the commands of others. Now, I have plenty of ways to deal with people like you.
rows.speaker: Wizened Priest

rows.text: I'm not sure whether I should laugh or cry right now... I can't believe that a follower such as you could have been made by a Creation Titan.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: As I see it, a dead Titan can't provide you with this level of confidence, right? Then who is it, exactly? Could it be Caenis?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You...
rows.speaker: Wizened Priest

rows.text: Hmph... Seeing how fond of you Elder Caenis is, I shall let that slide for now. Leave immediately and don't impede us from receiving the supreme being's blessings.
rows.speaker: Wizened Priest

rows.text: (Seeing as we were able to hear of this matter from the mouths of others, it seems that Caenis is indeed quite sincere toward us. Perhaps this affair will proceed smoother than I had anticipated...)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh my, what a thrilling confrontation... As expected of one of {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s followers.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: ...Are you praising or insulting him?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Praising him, of course. As a believer of the god of Deliverance, it is only natural that he detests evil.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Didn't you hear me? I asked you to leave! Go as far away from here as possible! Don't mutter to yourself like some sort of madman and disturb my meditation!
rows.speaker: Wizened Priest

rows.text: Every plant, every tendril, no, even every leaf could be the embodiment of {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}...
rows.speaker: Debating Scholar

rows.text: As a result, mere mortals who did not know what the Titan actually looked like chose to paint them as a giant tree instead. Their wisdom was portrayed as fruit to symbolize how they shared their knowledge equally among the masses... Such exquisiteness indeed!
rows.speaker: Debating Scholar

rows.text: This mural is quite abstract.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I really can't tell whether you are praising or demeaning yourself. Now I'm quite curious whether the Reason Titan has studied figures of speech before?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heheh, of course I find such stylistic devices interesting.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: For all we know, this could be the answer to the question, "What exactly are we?"
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hmph, I, for one, am not willing to admit that I could look this ugly.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heheh... Was this the reason why you failed in your attempt to refine my soul when you were ambushed at the Grove?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Since you are aware of this, why did you save me back then?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: From my perspective, this point alone was enough to separate you from the average person.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: ...How do two lunatics coexist in the same brain?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Therefore, it seems that your journey to Dawncloud this time is not just to seek protection...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: ...What, then, is the intention behind your actions?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: The entire plan is stored in my memory, so why don't you look there?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heheh, then don't mind if I do...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: One year old, two years old...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Oh my, even a member of the preeminent Seven Sages must hug his dromas doll to sleep? How interesting...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: ...That's enough.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: How unusual, your soul is actually trembling. This must mean that behind this toy hides a secret that nobody knows, right?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hmph... Since our days are both numbered, I don't mind telling you more about it.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: This is a present that my sister gave to me. It's a doll that was made to look like our family pet.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: So, there are other members in your family, eh? Are they also living in Okhema?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Don't you just love to pick through my brain? Go on, continue flipping through my memories.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: It won't take long... You'll discover the answer when you reach the memories of when I was five.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The black tide is everywhere... I can't bear to look.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text:
When I was young, I couldn't accept this outcome either. {RUBY_B#Earth Titan}Georios{RUBY_E#}, {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#},
{RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}... and you, of course. Although I prayed to every Titan that I could think of for help, my efforts were ultimately futile.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: This... Could this be the inception of your research into alchemy?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Indeed it was. Everything started from that verdant courtyard of yours. When I was pursuing my education there, I naturally also came to learn of {RUBY_B#The First Scholar}Thalesus'{RUBY_E#} theory as well.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh, I remember that person. He was the one to come up with the concept of "souls," right?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Not only that, he also believed that life, as well as the composition, movement, and transformation of matter, all stem from souls themselves. This is why I thought that...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Since all living things stemmed from the same origin, why could I not sacrifice myself in order to resurrect my nearest and dearest?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Anaxa, you...
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: I did it, teacher.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: B—But this is absolute blasphemy... Regardless of how much freedom the Grove provides, such an act could cause you to be burned at the pyre...!
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Your beloved... Where is she now? Send her away from the Grove at once, to a place where nobody will ever be able to find her. Otherwise, the both of us will be judged by the Council of the Seven Sages...!
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Calm down, teacher. My sister, she...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: She's still not in the mortal realm... even to this day.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What do you mean...?
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: It was naive of me to think that I could snatch the deceased from {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}' grip by merely sacrificing one eye...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Equivalent exchange... All I received for that price was but an opportunity to see her for one final time. Nothing more.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Let it go, Anaxa. As one of my best students, I cannot watch you go down the wrong path without doing anything to stop it.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Never do something taboo ever again. Don't disappoint the deceased and never harm yourself. If you can do that, this classroom will still be yours and you'll have a chance to live out your own life.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Since I was able to see her one last time, I have no other desires...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You're right, teacher. It's time for me to start a new life.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I am sincerely glad for you, child. Now then, what topic would you like to study?
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: I wish to continue Thalesus' research.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Continue the research into souls? But you know that the Grove has long since understood his philosophy like the back of their hands. Even if you continue digging into this subject, your efforts will likely be futile...
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: No, teacher. After my fleeting glimpse of the deathly fog, I finally understood a single truth: Since ancient days, our understanding of souls is but the tip of the iceberg.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I may have lost an eye, but my view of the world has become clearer than ever...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I have grasped the truth with my bare hands... Watch as I turn this farcical world upside down.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hmm... Who would have thought such a secret lay concealed beneath that hefty eye patch of yours?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: However, this story doesn't seem to be connected to your plan... In fact, I'd say that they aren't related at all?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: The answer lies within my tale. If even you cannot understand it, perhaps you should relinquish the divinity of Reason to me? After all, it'd be a waste for you to hold onto it.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: My story ends here. Now, it's time for you to tell me your secret. After all, this is what equivalent exchange means, correct?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: As expected, you laid a trap for me to step into...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Unfortunately, even if I was willing to talk about my past, I may not know more about it than you do.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Oh? Are you saying that the renowned Reason Titan is now admitting a lack of wisdom? Your followers are going to be sorely disappointed by this.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Child of humanity, remember this: Being cognizant of one's ignorance is the greatest wisdom of all.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Now I understand. No wonder you asked me to answer your random, nonsensical questions.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Not only that, you're the only one who can shed light on my query. As the saying goes, onlookers see most clearly.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hmph, is that so...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Lord Anaxa...!
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: Hmm...?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I saw you muttering to yourself and was wondering whether you were caught in a delirium of reflective thought? I'm sorry to interrupt you, but time is of the essence...
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: I have a message from Lord Lygus: Lady Caenis has met up with the Council of Elders and is awaiting your arrival, so please depart forthwith.
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: Hmph... It's finally time.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Kephale, the one who created the world, and the one who bears the world...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: If you truly have not met your end... how will you answer the challenges of those who defy you?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Lord Anaxagoras! I've heard so much about you...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Head of the Nousporists of the Grove of Epiphany, notorious blasphemer, a Chrysos Heir who bears {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}' Coreflame, a survivor of the Grove calamity...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Did I miss anything? If so, please be so kind as to enlighten me.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Since Lady Caenis is already well acquainted with me, I won't waste any effort introducing myself again.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But then again, perhaps the customs are different here? Back in my hometown, there is a form of etiquette known as "honoring guests": The host will welcome their guests with warm hospitality by treating them to fine wine and a cozy bed...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: And yet, ever since I arrived, I have not been welcomed with warm courtesy or ceremonial gifts. Instead, I am met with intense scrutiny. Even more absurd, the host has sharpened their blade and instructed their servants to lie in wait in the shadows...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Perhaps you intend to cut open my heart, retrieve the Coreflame, and then hold a grand feast for all of the guests?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Everyone, stand down.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Thank you for understanding. I am but a feeble scholar who is not used to the stench of avarice and blood.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: No need to be humble, my lord. From my perspective, your courage and gumption are worthy of the reputation of the Seven Sages. Your bravery is more than adequate to accomplish our perilous endeavor.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: So, you wish to start a war?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Well, since the Chrysos Heirs are calling for war, we will respond in kind. Conflict is inevitable. Since Aglaea endeavors to suppress the virtuous commoners with blood of gold, we will not hesitate to display the rights and mettle that the citizens of Okhema are so entitled to.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: As to your question of whether peace is still a viable option? Well, to that, I can only say this: Everything hinges on the next citizens' assembly and whether they have a sudden epiphany amid the clamor of the masses...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: ...And since you, as a Chrysos Heir, accepted our invitation, you have indeed given us a glimmer of hope.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Hah, what brazen arrogance. What you're saying right now is worlds apart from what you were saying before you retired your "cleaners."
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I don't deny it. After all, they're responsible for cleaning up any threats and just a moment ago, you were on the side of the Chrysos Heirs...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: ...But now that you're an ally of ours, we can continue talking somewhere else. As you know, these walls have ears.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Continuing from the earlier topic, let us discuss our common enemy: Aglaea.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: She is the second-most experienced Chrysos Heir across the whole of Okhema, who has gradually lost her humanity to the ravages of time and the ablation of the Coreflame... A formidable opponent indeed.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Admittedly, there is ample reason for her to take your life. Yet, your previous reasoning is quite sound. As a seasoned political animal, it's unclear whether she will actually cross that irreversible boundary. Moreover, she still needs you alive so that the Titan's trial can be completed...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Is there anyone present who can swear by the sacred vow of {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} and guarantee that you weren't in league with that woman before coming here? Are you just trying to pull the wool over our eyes and aid her in her savagery?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: As compared to a comprehensive plan with uncertain results, if you decide to cut open my chest and remove the Coreflame, wouldn't that settle her nerves even more? Everything is in place — she just needs the right timing.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Since I believe in neither Titans nor the prophecy, there's no way that I would willingly walk on the path that she extols. Given how rigorously she enforces her principles, how would she ever accept a heretic such as me?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: At the very least, the both of us agree that this tyrant who wallows in extravagance and greed is the greatest threat to achieving peace in Okhema. The Council of Elders is willing to defend your right to live, just as we defend every oppressed citizen.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: However, I regret to say that sentiments in favor of the Chrysos Heirs and Aglaea are only growing in magnitude. The peace that we are aspiring toward, as well as everything that we hold dear, will be destroyed completely. The city will be burned to ashes and the citizens' blood will be shed...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Tell me, what are you willing to do for our esteemed citizens so that they can vanquish the enemies of our fine city?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: The Council of Elders needs more backing if it wishes to topple Aglaea and it's evident that the academy wields considerable influence.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: At the very least, I have served as the Grove's special envoy to Okhema for a significant amount of time. Of course, this also means that I will hold a crucial vote at the citizens' assembly.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heh, surely you don't believe that such a tiny betrayal will be enough to push her to her wits' end?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: What's more, there are many who remain silent, merely watching to see how much chaos I can unleash... Not to mention, you know full well that the Chrysos Heirs have never been a united front.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: At this stage, it's clear that you and I understand the benefits to be won from this discussion. Let me put it plainly: The Council of Elders has always been renowned for its fairness, and that fairness is built on a foundation of sincerity...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: The Council of Elders has vowed to all citizens of Okhema that it will always remain loyal to them. As for you, my lord, how will you guarantee that you will be able to live up to such earnestness and will not betray Okhema's indomitable citizens when the opportunity presents itself, just as you now betray Aglaea when it suits you?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: I am incredibly honored to have witnessed the both of you bury the hatchet in a civilized manner. However, I'm afraid that I must interrupt for a brief moment...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: As the Theoros, I have observed the following: Lady Aglaea, the Goldweaver, is currently on her way to Dawncloud.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Oh? Well, I do believe that we might have a slight overabundance of guests today.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Feeling dissatisfied, Lady Caenis? Despite the Council of Elders' lofty residence on Dawncloud, it must still tolerate the whims of the Chrysos Heirs.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heh, so you were holding back just now? Seems like you are better at playing this game than I. In any case, I am glad that she's arriving here...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: So, tell me, Anaxagoras: Now that you're an ally of mine, if Aglaea were to demand that I hand you over, what should I do?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: You can do as she says. Tell her that the Council of Elders merely wished to chat with me and had no intention of offending her.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: However, by doing so, the authority of the Council of Elders will be as thin as papyrus that has been soaked in blood. Not only can it be destroyed at the slightest touch, but the Council will also lose possession of a valuable Coreflame...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: No, more like two Coreflames. After all...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: At the next citizens' assembly, {RUBY_B#Castorice}that young lady who is synonymous with death{RUBY_E#} will also be standing on our side.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh? How can you be sure of that?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Is that of importance to you? All you need to know is that I have a plan. In my opinion, you should be more worried about the impending threat.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: If Aglaea can seize me in full view of the masses today, she could also dismiss the entire Council of Elders in one fell swoop tomorrow. If that happens, the discussion that we've just had will turn into an utter joke instead...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Is this the outcome that you wish to see, Lady Caenis?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Fine, I will handle this matter appropriately.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: But you'd do best to remember this: Fool the people and karma will be on your tail. I'll overlook it this time, but don't count on there being a next time...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: ...Unless, of course, you crave cruel punishment and consider suffering the perfect state to ponder the true nature of souls.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Well, what do you know! That happens to be one of my rare talents.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: We shall see, then.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Ah, I've got to say that you've managed to really impress me again. But... shouldn't you be going after more?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Dying to know what I'm after, huh?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I mean... I'm the Reason Titan, after all. It is in me to ask and seek answers.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Easy there, you'll learn the answer soon enough.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I didn't bring it up with her purely because she doesn't have the means to give me what I truly want. It's as they say, onlookers see most clearly.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The true master of Dawncloud has always been the Theoros, who watches over everything.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...An expected visitor. Welcome, once again.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You know, you could actually skip all the pointless debate and come straight to me to seek an audience with {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I have no reason to refuse you, do I?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You may not, but Caenis has. Whoever gets hold of {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s Coreflame will get to rule over Okhema...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: She's wary of me, so naturally, I had to gain her trust. I would say that debate was not at all pointless.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Very true.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: In my view, this individual has gone to great lengths to get close to Kephale. He might very well be plotting something nefarious against the Titan.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Are you still willing to let him pass knowing this?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Yes, very much so. All living creations are always free to visit {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s transcendent vessel. This comes with being the Worldbearer.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Hmph, how convenient it is to be able to hear what they say...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: It is truly my honor to speak to a venerated Titan in person.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Please, go ahead. Let me join you both on this journey.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Go on ahead. Take this {RUBY_B#Janus's Hidden Passage}"Janus shortcut"{RUBY_E#} and the long pilgrimage stairway will be waiting for you at its end.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I have to admit I never expected you to not ask me anything, not even my motive.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Because I know very well what it is you are after. As the saying goes: A gentleman helps others achieve their goals. I have a feeling that your theory will be validated at the end of this journey—
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I believe {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} will not deprive you of your right to ask your question, especially now that you're on the brink of death... you must be closer to Kephale than anyone else, wouldn't you agree?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Ha... I hope things go as you say, then.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Putting a child of justice into a farcical world is bound to turn it upside down...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: It is my hope that you bring a much-needed change to this world which is on the brink of destruction.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Honestly, this is my first time going up to Dawncloud's peak...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What a splendid view... Isn't it about time you recognized the magnificence of us Titans?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hmph. Well, I don't see how this place is different from those temples in the city. All they have are magnificent facades...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: And even though I've come this far, I'm still doubtful about getting useful clues from him.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hmph... I must be getting ahead of myself to be expecting to hear something nice from you.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Oh? Haven't you been in my head for some time now? It's high time you get used to how I feel about things.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Alright, we're just a short hike away from {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}. No time to waste here...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Urk...!
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: So, the intellectual debate from earlier was too draining for you, huh... If Amphoreus gets a new lease on life, you should focus on strengthening your body and stop shirking social interactions.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: ...Save your concern.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The Titan is in sight. Can you make it?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Pfft... Why? Are you going to carry me up if I were to fall now?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I know how far I can go, so just hold your tongue and come along.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Fine, then. I guess I won't say any more. I'll just wait till your soul dissipates completely to gain control over your body.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: (Wait, who is that...? {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}?)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hey, look at that...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hm? What should I be looking at?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: (Am I hallucinating...?)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: (Or do we even get to see souls when we're close to dying...?)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh? Why didn't you bring your favorite spear with you on this trip, Gnaeus?
(Gnaeus? I know I've heard this name somewhere...)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Ah, it's unfortunate...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: The black tide destroyed every last inch of my Kalyx.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: How could that be...?
Even a creation of {RUBY_B#Earth Titan}Georios{RUBY_E#}, from their prized ores and molten fire, couldn't escape the fate of destruction...?
Hey, {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}... Do you know a certain Gnaeus?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Gnaeus? No, not that I remember. How did you even think up such a strange name?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I just saw him. Gnaeus... a warrior-like figure who was just chatting with you here...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: No, I have no such memory. Could you be hallucinating?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hngh... Ugh...
Can you keep going?
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: O—Of course... I'm just...
Tsk... If I knew we had to climb a mountain, I wouldn't have come along with you...
I guess this also counts as one aspect of the Worldbearing burden. If Amphoreus does have a next life, you may want to get your body in shape.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Keep your sarcasm to yourself...
(Tsk... I'm not getting anything of value from them.)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I... would sooner throw myself off this cliff and hit rock bottom... than exercise even a little.
I... I am Calypso of the eminent Seven Sages, after all... Training would make me no different from those Helkolithist barbarians...!
rows.speaker: Calypso

rows.text: (Calypso? She's one of the Seven Sages... A member of the Grove?)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: (No, she can't be. I would know her name if she really were one of the Seven Sages...)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hey, Cerces! Does the name Calypso ring a bell?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...Hm? {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: We're here, finally. So, I don't get to ask the Titan my question, but all of you make for a pleasant surprise, nonetheless.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Very well, then. Let me uncover the truth for myself...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Urk...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Did I... still fail to make it in time...?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...Huh?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: So, I'm back here again...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: This is...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I can hear it.
I hear it, from the depths of the tides, behind the closed doors of {RUBY_B#nether realm}the void world{RUBY_E#} — a voice ready to tell me something—
This time, the voice is a lot clearer than before.
Tsk...
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Since we've come this far, let's just wait.
rows.speaker: Calypso

rows.text: Lord Gnaeus and Miss Calypso? Are you both here to visit Khaos too?
Yes, and we've been waiting for quite some time now...
rows.speaker: Calypso

rows.text: Regrettably, he hasn't answered us.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: The worst-case scenario is that he's... already been overwhelmed and crushed by the Worldbearing burden.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: You're overthinking, Lord Gnaeus. I can still sense Khaos' soul in the area.
And besides, we both know Khaos' nature. A Deliverer like him wouldn't fall so readily, much less give up on all that he holds dear, isn't that so?
Yes, I have faith in him.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: That reminds me. Why are you making this trip alone, Polyxia?
rows.speaker: Calypso

rows.text: Oh, my sister needs more time to make sure the flowers are fine...
rows.speaker: Polyxia

rows.text: Heh...
rows.speaker: Calypso

rows.text: Such a pity... Both of you have hearts kinder than anyone else, yet you are born only to take over {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}'s divinity.
rows.speaker: Calypso

rows.text: Everything that I see and hear this time has left me shaken to the core.
What may seem like a mundane conversation is, in truth, a once-in-a-lifetime exchange that has revealed the ultimate answer to {RUBY_B#What exactly are we?}Cerces' question{RUBY_E#}.

The conjecture has taken shape and must now be solidified into a theorem. Next, I only need to seek verification from {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}. By doing so, I can answer {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}' question and reclaim my body...
...But no, I will not do that. That isn't important.
