Because another one of my conjectures — one that I have always dreamed of proving — has been proven right this very instant.
Fusing a mortal's soul with that of a Titan to replace said Titan... is not a ludicrous idea after all.
Enough about me. Did Khaos ever reply to you?
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Ahh, well, regrettably...
...Seems like the price of becoming a demigod is a lot heftier than we thought.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: (Khaos? Demigod?)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: (I've never heard of this person... Which Titan's authority did he inherit?)
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Look on the bright side, Gnaeus. Since we've come all this way, I doubt he'd snub his old friends, would he?
Hmph... Let's just hope we mean as much as the world to him.
rows.speaker: Gnaeus

rows.text: Hey? Are you seeing that same hallucination again?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Yes... It's still you and Gnaeus, but you're now talking about a certain Khaos. I'm guessing he's one of your companions?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Khaos? This name sounds just as strange to me...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Never mind, I think I know what this is about. If things are as I thought, then they aren't hallucinations, but...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The souls of people.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Wha... But if those are the souls of the dead, then what am I?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hmph, beats me... For all I know, you're just an illusion I conjured up in my dying moments.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Let's just keep going. As long as I take in more sights and hear more stories...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Know your limits. Wander too far among the dead and even I might not be able to save you.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: A book covered in annotations from many scholars. Its title is The Art of Sophistry: 40 Ways to Improve Your Debating Skills.

You skim through it, and the highlighted methods include virtual causation, false premises, contradiction conversion, conflating prevarication and reality, misinterpreted punctuation, misattribution, and generalizing specificity, among others.

Amidst it are scholars' exclamations: "A true eye-opener, the art of language knows no bounds," "If I can't master sophistry, I can at least learn to defend myself against them as an honest man," and so on.
The last resort is... "When all else fails, employ brute force."
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...This isn't going to be of any help, that's for sure.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: A record of the many research topics a Caprist scholar had applied for, and the replies from their school's Sage about these topics...

Topic 1: A discovery that many mythical beasts renowned for their longevity actually reside in areas with poorly managed birth and death records for such creatures. Permission to research. Reply: Lacks research significance, not approved.

Topic 2: An observation of real plants within the Grove imitating the growth patterns of nearby White Dryads. Permission to research. Reply: Falls under the domain of the Lotophagist school, not approved.
Topic 3: Investigating the feasibility of placing flying birds into rocket tubes to guide the direction of the rocket's flight. Permission to research. Reply: Too fanciful, not approved.
...The subsequent topics grew increasingly eclectic, yet the outcome of the replies remained unchanged.
Impressive tenacity... Hopefully it helped him survive the black tide.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (In the myths, Aquila, the Titan who reigns over the domain of the skies, is a colossal bird that overlooks the world beneath them with a hundred eyes. As long as they continue to soar above the clouds, the people of Amphoreus will remain trapped on the ground...)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (In Amphoreus, Titans are a common topic of discussion. People create myths that, in turn, conceive Titans... It's a tricky task to keep an objective view when among the people of Amphoreus.)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (Nobody could've ever imagined that [Trailblazer]'s life would be forfeited the moment we landed on Amphoreus...)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The clock is ticking... I should search for clues as I move.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (Titans and Aeons are two distinct classes of beings. Titans can communicate with us humans, and it is not impossible for us to overpower them. Upon their demise, we can even take over their divinity.)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (Chrysos Heirs are humans who possess heroic qualities, with most of them demonstrating extraordinary combat prowess and strength. Upon clearing a Coreflame trial, a Chrysos Heir can even ascend to a demigod and inherit a Titan's divinity...)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (Guided by the prophecy, the heroes are on a quest to reclaim Coreflames and usher in the Era Nova. Their efforts have seen gratifying results to date.)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (I should probably turn my attention to something else.)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The Grove of Epiphany is home to seven schools of thought. While all seven schools are founded on the ideologies of Thalesus the First Scholar, each is unique in its own way. Among them, the Venerationists revere and worship the Titans the most.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Nearly everyone in Amphoreus has heard the story of the skyships by now. {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#}'s stature is loftier than the heavens, and their divine retribution is merciless.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Nousporists primarily study the application of alchemy in soul repair.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Anaxa often says that... "Every failure brings us one step closer to the truth."
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: As told in the myths, the seas, the skies, and the earth are all, beyond the shadow of a doubt, creations of the Titans.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Based on the history of the Flame-Chase Journey, humans have the potential to take over the divinity of Titans.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Needless to say, his critics didn't take kindly to his answer, so they followed up with a second allegation.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: From the Abyss of Fate to Castrum Kremnos, I've seen many a Titan creation during my time in Amphoreus. Lifeforms created by {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} can also be found in the Grove.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Anaxa seems to hold special interest in the divinity coursing through the Chrysos Heirs' veins, and has even conducted a thorough investigation into the heroes' backgrounds.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Through alchemy, Anaxa aims to refine the golden blood in the Chrysos Heirs to a degree of purity equal to "divinity."
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What are you thinking about?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Just amazed at how this towering tree is {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}'s divine body. It's a majestic sight.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Is that so? You don't look the slightest bit amazed, though. Plus, you seem to be strangely familiar with the city around the Great Tree...?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: ...Merely something from the past that I won't go in to.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Events of the past, huh... I was also a child when I looked up at {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}. Their leaves and branches reflected the sparkling stars, and their trunk was like a pillar that supported the sky and ground.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: I stood at this very spot back then, imagining the day when I could climb to the top of this tree... Because I would be the closest I can be to the sky at that spot.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: You're a Sky Priest, yet you study at a place that is home to the Reason Titan... That's rather counterintuitive.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Don't read too much into it. I mean, can mortals even hope to reach {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila's{RUBY_E#} realm? They're a strict and draconian god, nothing like {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}. Reason is willing to share what is theirs with others, but Sky... only expects people to revere them.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: You get what I'm saying, right Dannie? After all, the Titan that imprisoned you and [Trailblazer] here in Amphoreus is none other than {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#} themself...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Yes, I didn't count on provoking the ire of a local god.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: But there will always be people who dream of soaring toward the sky. The Grove has a wealth of research on {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#}, and that is exactly what we are here for.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: It's just... I never thought Grayie would meet with something like that before we set off... As a physician, I should have been there by {M#his}{F#her} side.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Bad luck tends to come in streaks, so don't beat yourself up over it. Besides, Aglaea needs you here to uncover the truth behind what happened to the Grove. Let's just make the most out of this trip and keep a lookout for any documents related to the Death Titan. They could be useful to [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yeah... There's no rest for the weary, huh.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: In any case, what we're looking for could be anywhere in this enormous Grove. Let's split up to cover more ground. Dannie, with your skills, I'm sure those monsters born of the black tide will pose no threat to you anyway.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: What about you? Will you be alright on your own?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hehe, have you forgotten that you're talking to the chief physician of the Twilight Courtyard? Have more faith in me. I'll be just fine!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: ...The silence in here is near deafening.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: With the vast amount of knowledge it holds, this academy is akin to a labyrinth of information... Even the cleverest of scholars would easily lose their way in here. I should gather my thoughts before heading in.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (Hyacine's forebears were priests who worshiped {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#}. Nobody is more familiar with the taboos of the Sky Titan than her. Seeing how Aglaea has sent her here as a guide, it's possible that she plans to have Hyacine take on a trial in the future.)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (Is there a way to step out of the situation and look at it from a different perspective?)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (In this regard, Titans can be said to be a lot more similar to humans than Aeons are...)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (Wait, something about that feels off. Is this a... selection process of some sort?)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (As I expected, the prophecy is the hardest to make any sense of. But with barely any information to go on, no matter how much I ruminate on it, it won't yield any results... I should leave this for another time.)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (I should have done more to keep {M#him}{F#her} safe... but it's not too late. We still have a fighting chance. The unique rules that govern life and death on Amphoreus might just work in our favor and save {M#him}{F#her}.)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: (The Grove is a veritable library of knowledge... Maybe they'll have records on a similar case? Please let there be one...)
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That's... Hyacine? Why is she surrounded by so many monsters? ...As much faith as I have in her, it's probably a good idea to help her out there.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Really now? This is way more trouble than I could've asked for.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Need a hand?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hm... Or you could sit back and watch?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: I can't tell if you're serious or not... But being hard to read isn't without its perks, I suppose.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hehe, I'm kidding, Dannie! Lend me a hand, pretty please? Alright, now let's get them!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Anaxa... goras. He's the scholar who fused himself with the Coreflame of Reason.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: This is new. I didn't know Professor Anaxa was researching the Sky. He's never mentioned anything about it.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Phainon said Anaxa might be opposed to the Flame-Chase Journey.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: "Might" is an understatement. Anaxa has never been one to venerate the gods, nor has he ever found it within himself to put any faith in the prophecy. People have come to think of him as a heretic, even in a place as liberal as the Grove.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Yet, it is also this very "blasphemer" that {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} favors. Fate sure works in mysterious ways.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: I picked up a scroll on my way here, too. It looks like it may be related to the one you're holding.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Oh? Let me have a look.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Hyacine combines both records together...
By the looks of them, these scrolls are records of two conversations that took place in the same setting, one after the other.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: There's still much I don't know about the Grove. Do you mind if I ask you a few questions?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Sure, go ahead.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: As the sage of the Venerationists, Euthyphro has always been at loggerheads with Anaxa.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: If we were to place the Seven Sages on the scales of {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#}, Anaxa and Euthyphro would be placed on opposite sides to achieve balance.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: A very illustrative explanation. Thank you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That's why it's no use building giant sky-faring ships... Oh, but I do wonder if a supercharged mini Tribbie cannon could slip past their watch?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: That was a joke... right?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Everyone considers Anaxa a blasphemer, but that has never stopped him from sharing his ideas, no matter how taboo. If you must say that he's hiding something... then it's likely what lies beneath his eye patch.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Perhaps, to him, the crash of the skyship carries a different interpretation. The firmament is not impenetrable. On the contrary, it was precisely because the skyship represented the first step toward breaking free from the shackles of the earth that it provoked the wrath of the Sky Titan and brought divine punishment upon itself.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: It's a shame that the majority of the Grove's research on {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#} was headed by the Venerationists, with sacrificial rituals making up a predominant part of their findings. Discourse about more esoteric subject matters in relation to {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#} dwindled even further after the skyship incident, so much so that even this scroll is completely new to me.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Don't worry about it. We'll just collect everything we can find on the Titans for now.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There's something else that's caught my attention, though... This says that Anaxa is conducting secret experiments of some sort?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That's what I'd like to know. What are these experiments he's involved in? Even I, the assistant lecturer, know next to nothing about them...
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: This is the Library of Philia, a place where the Grove stores its collection of tomes.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Other than books written by the seven schools, you can also find philosophical texts, ballads, and religious writings from the outlands here. Cities that desired to learn from the Grove were apparently expected to contribute knowledge of equal value to what they sought.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: We've had more than our fair share of hilarious episodes over the years. For instance, it's said that the Erythrokeramists once borrowed a manuscript from a certain author but ended up returning a copy instead of the original! What's more, the original manuscript was supposedly then hidden here.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: That... doesn't seem like a nice thing to do.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Nice? No need to hold yourself back, Dannie. You can just tell it like it is: Their behavior was no different from bandits!
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Well, if you don't mind: Did the Grove ever rob Castrum Kremnos?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You've got me there. Some said you couldn't even find a dictionary in Castrum Kremnos, so I guess they were spared.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: There are too many books in the Library of Philia. Flipping through them all will take too long. Why don't we use the biblioslate to search for the texts we need? We can bring them back to Okhema for reading after that.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Agreed, this place isn't safe. We should leave as soon as we're done.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There are still several more scrolls strewn all over the place. I'll gather them while you pull up those texts, this way, nothing will be overlooked.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: This is the place, but... where is everything?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Materials for alchemical experiments, matrix diagrams, and even the seal to the lab... They're all gone. Did the black tide destroy it all?
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: No wonder we didn't see any defense mechanisms along the way.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Have you ever been here before?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: No, not even close. Not only are alchemy experiments high-risk activities, but Professor Anaxa also has a penchant for using bizarre materials. Students often saw him walk in looking right as rain but come out covered in soot with his hair singed. Naturally, no one dared to come near this place.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Huh? That bookshelf over there seems to be the only thing still intact.
rows.speaker: Hyacine

rows.text: Sir, this sky above us... It's not real, is it?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Of course not. This is just an image from a projection device used for educational purposes. A simple trick.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: The day-night cycle has been lost to this world. So that students like you may still learn about the night sky, astronomers have harnessed the Titans' miraculous power to manipulate the light, projecting the "nights of the past" here for you.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Much like how the sky above the holy city is also illuminated by {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s Dawn Device.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: So, the skies of Okhema are fake, too.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You mustn't conclude that, Anaxa. You should know that only a child would expose a trick and be proud of it.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Often, people know more than they let on. They simply choose to feign ignorance because they have no other choice.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Then they're just deluding themselves. People believe in {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s tale of genesis, accepting wholesale whatever the priests preach, but we're different. We've already walked out of the fire-lit cave of ignorance.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: We have already realized that we live in a world where Titans make the rules. Even when we look at the sky, we're only seeing what they allow us to see. Rather than gazing at this mockery of a night sky fabricated by them for the rest of my life, why shouldn't I be the one to take control of the projection device instead?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: So much time has passed since you sowed the seeds of doubt in my heart, child. Many a night, I find myself penning down all my theories and wild ideas, only to burn them to ashes when I open my eyes in the day.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Why? Because we'll face death by burning if word gets out?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: As a sage of the Venerationists, my soul has already become inextricably linked to the Great Tree. Every word I say and every move I make is certain to influence every leaf, every branch... even the Tree itself.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: But above all else, my days are numbered. Instinctively, I have my doubts about the golden blood and the human soul, yet I have no means of verifying them. The golden blood in my veins is woefully thin, and I am loath to waste what little time I have left obsessing over a hypothesis that cannot even be proven in the first place.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: But I can, sir! I can do it for us! The time is right. Give me all that I need, and I shall accomplish this grand feat on your behalf.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You're right. I shall do just that. In the next meeting of the sages, I will spare no efforts fighting for the rights you deserve.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Go. Establish your own school of thought...
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Find out what we are... become the one who conquers the ultimate truths of the world.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Child of humanity...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: You didn't go to such lengths for an audience with {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} just to ask him a few questions, did you?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hmph. So you figured it out.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: If I were as foolish as a dromas, perhaps I'd throw myself down and prostrate before their greatness, begging for the gods' prophetic wisdom. Well, sorry to disappoint, but I'm no dromas. Alas, I am a human, standing tall on two feet, possessing both intellect and pride.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heh... Before such power, does it make any difference whether you're a human or a dromas?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I'm sure you're familiar with the story of the Styxians. When the raging waves threatened to swallow them, they didn't just give up and become sitting ducks. No, they constructed a dam that kept the roaring tide at bay, chaining down the mad {RUBY_B#Ocean Titan}Phagousa{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: They call me a blasphemer, Cerces, but that doesn't mean I deny the existence of gods. It's just...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...As I see it, Titans are simply a force that mankind has yet to find a way to tame.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh? If power that rivals the Titans' is what you crave, why not conform to the prophecy and brave the trial?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hah, why stop at harnessing the power of the Titans when I can do so much more?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The source of life is what I wish to grasp... To understand what makes up the soul, and to learn what we really are.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Thanks to you, I've had the chance to personally verify — in more ways than one — that the soul indeed ceases to exist in "Death." But where there is death, there is life, and where there is an end, there must also be a beginning.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: How, then, is a soul born? That was the only unknown variable left in my calculations.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: And by the sound of it, you have already formed a conjecture.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: No, I have already drawn a conclusion. In my journey unto death just now, I finally saw the answer with my own eyes.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Professor Anaxa...
I'm here. [Trailblazer]'s life hangs by a thread, I must ask you to refrain from taking any unnecessary steps.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Of course, I'll bring this to a conclusive end and give you the answer you so desire.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: However, in accordance with the principle of "equivalent exchange," I must also demand from you what I need.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...As you wish.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Don't you care to know what the price might be?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: It's a matter of uncovering the truth about the Death Titan — and [Trailblazer]'s survival...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This may be the only time I can ever save someone's life. There is no need for me to think twice.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I see. In that case... let the show begin.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Indulge me: Am I correct to say that you intend to prove {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}' whereabouts and prove the nature of our existence now?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Before I begin, I must confess I had been stuck in a cognitive trap all this time.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: As unrelated as these two propositions may seem at first glance, they are, in fact, logical equivalents. They are merely two different ways of telling us about what the soul is at its core.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The reason I say this is as I've mentioned earlier: The answer was hidden in my journey unto death.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Professor... you were in the nether realm?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yes — I am but a living dead man now — but that's not important. What truly matters is — I overheard a conversation between heroes.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: That's not all... Remember how I said you were a part of that conversation too, {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: And I've told you that I have no recollection of such an event. That was likely just an illusion conjured up by the mind of a dying man.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Of course you wouldn't remember.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Because that wasn't you. That was Calypso, one of the Seven Sages of the Grove.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...Calypso?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That's the name I made up on a whim when speaking to this girl. How do you know of it?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: And surely you jest. Don't you think I, of all people, would know if that were the name of one of the Seven Sages under the shade of my tree? Don't you claim to know the Grove's past like the back of your hand?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: It seems you've lost even the memories seared into your soul.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Use your head, Cerces. Since all of this took place in the realm of the dead, it stands to reason their likenesses are of souls from the past.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The living cannot step foot into that world, so who could they be? Think about Calypso. Why does she share your likeness, yet you have no idea who she is?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The answer is evident, is it not?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Those fallen heroes are the mortal incarnations of the Titans before their ascensions to godhood. The gods aren't master creators born out of thin air, and they are no different from humans — because they all evolved from one.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hmm...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Does this answer disappoint you?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Yes, because you've answered nothing. If I truly was once human as you claim, then where do the children of humanity come from?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Even on the off chance that you speak the truth, this brings us no closer to grasping {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}' whereabouts. How are we to find them?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Heh, I knew you would say that.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But it matters not. I know what I'm doing. Actually, why don't we have this supreme being standing before us tell us everything?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You can revive a Titan?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Humans cannot return from the dead. Neither can gods.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But all we need to do is look at this from a different perspective, and the problem will resolve itself. The solution is simple: Just like what you did to me...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: If I'm reborn as {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}, I can rebuild the world and all within it as they once did. Simple, is it not?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh, please! Dear Gray Mystery, I'm not giving you broken seashells people used in the markets millennia ago...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: N—No! Your soul is almost gone for good...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: M—Me too.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Her payment was in gold and precious stones, which only covers the living passenger. You need to pay me as a member of the dead.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: You know, you're not wrong. At least it's a part of my responsibilities.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: I have lived a longer life than most people. Though I'm not as good at doing business as Lady Aglaea, I still have some savings.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Okay, okay! I didn't know you hold grudges, Gray Mystery.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Waaaah, I'm so scared! Tee-hee, can you even catch my tail?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Here, catch!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Totally. The trio team is the best set up to reach the finals.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: No need. I already told her. She's fine with it.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Hey, I'm just trying to make this journey feel more special, okay? Don't read too much into it.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Hey, that was a different purchase. Look, I'm just trying to make this journey feel more special.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Don't worry... it's not a lot...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Alright! Pass me the coin — it's time to get the god's powers going! A fleet-footed trip to the nether realm, here we come!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: With that... I won't have any regrets.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Ah! I...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Currently...
That's... a lot to take in at once.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hmph...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Lady Aglaea, please, let me explain.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Go on.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: You know that the Coreflame of "Death" has always been the greatest unknown regarding the Era Nova, which is why both you and Caenis desire to gain the power to control that Coreflame in the approaching citizens' assembly.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Professor Anaxa has come to a consensus with Caenis — They want to suspend the trial once {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}' Coreflame is reclaimed, hoping thus to eradicate "Death" from this world. If they're successful, then the Flame-Chase Journey will cease, and Okhema can enjoy everlasting peace.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But I know this runs counter to your wishes. So long as we do not usher in Era Nova, the black tide will never be eradicated. Even with Lord Mydei on the front line, and the black tide not posing an immediate risk, the danger nevertheless remains...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Honestly, it's difficult for me to assess the pros and cons in this decision... But someone must bring the Coreflame before we can begin negotiations over it.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The Titan could be very near. I cannot let this chance slip by. Besides... someone has to make this trip to bring back {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer]'s soul.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Well said.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: You already had every reason to seek an audience with {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}. It's that Great Performer who has weaponized your wishes and placed us in this difficult situation.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: A world without "Death"... Do you desire that, too?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: If fate dictates that my path must oppose yours, I will do all I can to resist it, and protect what I aspire to achieve.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Heh...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Lord Mydei showed me that without taking the first step, all talk of what follows is moot.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Styxia... I've visited that place in the past. Though it is now an island surrounded by the River of Souls' torrents, it's not hard to see its former splendor...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Go. I will not stand in your way. As for [Trailblazer]... you are someone who has cheated death. I believe you have more than enough reason to make the trip with Castorice and meet the god of "Death" themself.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Castorice, I too look forward to your journey. I wonder what kinds of new interpretations your completed story will bring to the Flame-Chase Journey.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...Thank you, Lady Aglaea.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I hate to put a damper on this heartwarming moment, but...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: If Styxia is now "an island surrounded by the River of Souls' torrents," then how do we find a way in? Lady Tribbie is probably...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The answer is quite simple.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: In the myths, {RUBY_B#Trickery Titan}Zagreus{RUBY_E#} once made the domain of the dead their treasure vault — that is to say, they could enter and leave the nether realm as they pleased.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: And if they could do that... then it follows that the demigod who inherited their divinity must be capable of the same.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I'll see you at Marmoreal Palace at {RUBY_B#noon}Action Hour{RUBY_E#} tomorrow. Cipher shall be your guide to finding that ancient city.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Later, somewhere in Okhema...
Cas? What a surprise.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Lady Tribbie...?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Is something troubling you?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...I just wanted to speak to Lady Trianne for a bit before I set off.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: No matter how breathtakingly beautiful Styxia once was, the place is now the domain of the departed... There is no telling what we'll encounter there.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I... don't want to have any regrets.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Has anyone told you that your eyes are sparkling today?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Is that a figure of speech...?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: In the past... When you did smile once in a while, all of us could see that your heart remained troubled even as you smiled.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Lady Tribbie, you know perfectly well... that see you tomorrow is nothing but a white lie.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I hope your toughness is not a mask hiding a lonely heart.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Cas... You hardly ever talked of your past. None of us knows what you went through apart from Agy. But we know it must have been filled with pain and hardships, as it is the fate every Chrysos Heir is destined to live out.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...We are just happy for you that the Coreflame you're meant to inherit has finally surfaced.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Isn't it a little too soon to say that?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But you already know where "tomorrow" is, don't you?
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: There is no need to rely on anyone else. Just give it your all and leave no regrets. We have always believed that your embrace is just as warm as everyone else's.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Because we embrace others to comfort them, and Cas... you're the kindest Chrysos Heir we know.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: ...Thank you, Lady Tribbie.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This feeling... It's hard to put into words. I suddenly found myself with so many wishes... so much I want to accomplish before setting off.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Then go do it, Cas!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: Trianne... was actually working on a surprise gift for you. It's a pity she didn't get to finish it, but now Trinnon and I are working on it, and we'll make sure to give it to you.
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: So, let's meet back here when you return from Styxia. Safe travels — see you tomorrow!
rows.speaker: Tribbie

rows.text: At the same time...
(I can't sleep...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: *Door knocks*
(...Hm? Who could it be?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I hope I didn't wake you.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: If it isn't too much to ask, I'd really like it if you could come along with me to retrieve something.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Ah, sorry! I didn't realize it was a joke.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I want to vote! Tell me how I can vote!
rows.speaker: Enraged Oronyx Devotee

rows.text: Take your ceramic shard engraved with the {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} rune, select the Council of Elders in your heart, and pray silently until the shard registers your choice. Then toss it into the dolium.
rows.speaker: Rational Talanton Devotee

rows.text: The Council of Elders? More like the council of buffoons! The black tide took my hometown long ago! Who are they kidding with bringing back Era Chrysea? It's all a sham to create their own Era Chrysea in Okhema!
rows.speaker: Enraged Oronyx Devotee

rows.text: The Titans are just... So long as we do not overstep our bounds again, we will not incur divine wrath.
rows.speaker: Rational Talanton Devotee

rows.text: Oh, please. The time when these deranged Titans should have vacated their spot to the demigods is long overdue! You'll see soon enough, you old fogey!
rows.speaker: Enraged Oronyx Devotee

rows.text: And I pray that {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#} smacks some sense into you with their scales. We shall see how this turns out!
rows.speaker: Rational Talanton Devotee

rows.text: That was... quite a spectacle.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This peaceful sight is making me forget that this is the end times.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Before coming here, I had lived for many years in Aidonia, a city of rime and frost. The people there were devotees of {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}, and were well-known for their unique burial rites and traditions.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Traditions that I played a major role in.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But back in those days, I was Aidonia's Maiden of War.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I was trudging across the frosty plains on my own when the Aidonians found me. They saw the curse in me as a blessing from {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}, and believed that my hands could correct the Era Chrysea's mistake and lead them to meet the great god of death.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: They provided me shelter, but in return...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I was expected to grant "merciful deaths" to war captives, prisoners bound for execution, and heroes alike.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Let's put that aside for the moment. We've arrived.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I want to retrieve a small gift I specially prepared for you. I made it myself, like the trinket I gave Lady Trianne... I want to leave something for everyone, if possible.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The journey to seek an audience with the Death Titan cannot be an easy one... I want to make full use of every moment I have before we depart, so that I don't have any regrets.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Where... did it go?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: What's... going on...?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Hmm? What's this...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Hmm? What's this...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The coin of {RUBY_B#Trickery Titan}Zagreus{RUBY_E#}, and a slate...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: So it's her.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: So many years have passed, yet she's still announcing herself in such a... "crass" manner.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Let's just do as the slate says and look for Lady Cipher.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Grumph...
rows.speaker: Cipher?

rows.text: Cipher — if this dromas truly is her — appears to be quite content, her gaze filled with three parts sincerity, three parts approval, three parts triumph, and three parts "Hahah, Gray Mystery, you've lost if you take this seriously."
She seems to be saying, "Hello."
Seeing you treat the dromas with such seriousness, all twelve parts of her complex emotions immediately transformed into one of admiration.
She seems to be saying, "Right. Oh, no, yeah yeah, yes."
After a moment of inner conflict, she reached a definitive conclusion: The dromas is indeed a cat.
She seems to be saying, "Ah hahah, Cipher does not know."
Hmm, so. She says she doesn't know.
Tsk. You're still careless as ever. Shouldn't you keep such a precious gift near your bosom?
rows.speaker: Cipher?

rows.text: Since you know it's a gift for someone else, please give it back to me. Stop hiding among the people and letting the wind carry your voice.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Now, now. Since I know it's a gift — That just means I need to milk its worth! The children of the wind never stay for long in one place, unless your offer is tempting enough to still the wind. What say you?
rows.speaker: Cipher?

rows.text: Name your price. I'll give you however much you want.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Ah... I'm sorry. Bargaining is really not my forte...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Hahaha! No wonder they call you Princess Homebody!
rows.speaker: Cipher?

rows.text: Tell you what, why don't you two come over to my place? It'll make a better venue for proper business discussions. You can find where I live through the winds I've sown, right?
rows.speaker: Cipher?

rows.text: Piece of cake... I can do that even if I can only sense your soul.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Alright, I'll see you there! Oh, by the way...
rows.speaker: Cipher?

rows.text: Everyone cool with me collecting a deposit before we reach an agreement, right? Hehe. Now, come this way...
rows.speaker: Cipher?

rows.text: The Dew of Divine Blood in the backpack has been stolen.
(Where did my Dew of Divine Blood go...!?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Ugh, she's incorrigible... Follow me!
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Over here, over here! ...No, not that way. This way!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Come on. If I really wanted to hide, you'd never find me.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: So, relax, you two! No need to get your hackles up. I'm not that scary, am I? Meow!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Give me the jewelry piece first... or everything's off the table.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Mind your own business.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Look! Isn't the view here just great? You can see what everyone is doing and where they're going, and they won't even know you're here.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Now that we've broken the ice, let's get to the point — Everything I've said so far has been a joke. I'm inviting you two here for three things:
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: One, the seamstress found me and wants me to take you to Styxia to look for the Death Titan.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Two... Ha, the Council of Elders also found me and wants me to make sure the Coreflame of {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} ends up in their hands.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: I'm telling you that I'm not interested in doing either of those things.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Don't go look for the Death Titan. The end.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Some time ago...
Whoa, this is some high-quality stuff...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: And this room is full of it... How much are these worth, hmm? Did you get all of this through that Era Nova gimmick?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Some of it is family fortune, while the rest came from my business as a dressmaster. Don't liken the Flame-Chase work to your shady dealings.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Wow... I should have busted down your door instead of going around like a thief.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Well, spill. Why are you giving me so much money?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Payment for doing work. You're worth this much.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Did you forget my stance to all this? I thought I made myself very clear.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: You wish to run away. Run away from your responsibilities, from the prophecy, and from your destiny. "You shall walk with greed, and die over petty change."
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I understand this prophecy weighs on you immensely. That is why I have never reproached the demigod of Trickery for running away.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: But I need you right now, so don't turn me down.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Hmm...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: You know, maybe the gods got your tongue with their golden threads, Aglaea. I'm not hearing any sincerity in your words.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Give me a reason why you're bowing your noble head to me.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: ...We lost Trianne.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Oh...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: The divine power of Passages is running out. I need another demigod to escort Castorice and help her fulfill her lifelong wish.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Oh, I get it now. You're sending Castorice to her death, and you want me to die with her.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: This is Castorice's own request. I have never seen her so determined.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: She... brought this up herself? You're not pulling my leg?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: She's also made up her mind to leave her confused past behind.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: ...As will you, Cipher, when you finally make up your mind.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Don't be so sure. Time has hardened the likes of you and I, but Castorice remains pure as driven snow.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: She can always turn back before the end, you know? Maybe she'll remember Trianne's sacrifice. Maybe she'll remember the countless martyred Chrysos Heirs. Maybe she'll remember you, with your one foot in the grave — I ain't as optimistic as you about what she'll want to do.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Tell you what, why don't I take this room of treasures as a security deposit and we make a bet?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Go on.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I bet she'll change her mind and turn back. Now, if I lose, I'll do what you want me to do, return this deposit to you, plus giving you another roomful of treasures. How does that sound?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: You sound like you have all the confidence in the world.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: In that case, let's make a pact with those conditions. I hope you're prepared to lose it all.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Mmm! Bright and sunny, just the weather for farewells.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: You're... here.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Tsk tsk, you sure know how to put me in a spot, Castorice... I need to travel with you, but I can't touch you. What a bother.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Sorry...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Aw, I was just teasing. Don't take it to heart.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Did you know that the legends say you have to put an {RUBY_B#little silver coin}obol{RUBY_E#} into the mouth of the dead or over their eyes if you want them to successfully cross the River of Souls and enter the nether realm?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: That's the ferry fare for entering the nether realm. However, I honestly won't ask you to pay this time. I'll pay. And then we'll just have to go through the motions...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Oh, one last thing before we go. I gotta give you this piece of advice, especially to you, Princess Homebody —
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: You can't catch the wind by waiting. You only live once, so make the most of every moment you have.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: But now... perhaps I might have one last chance.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Long ago, Trinnon read a prophecy to me: "At the end of the sea of flowers, the souls of the living shall warm thy fingertips, and after an embrace... there shall be eternal separation."
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I found no surprise in it, for her words sounded not like a foretelling, but a perfect reflection of my past.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Embraces in this world are born of reunions, yet my touch speaks only of farewells. In that moment, I had no doubt that this destiny would weave itself through the entirety of my life...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: And yet things have taken a turn for the better: Now that I can finally have an audience with {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}, perhaps I can rewrite the meaning of that fated prophecy.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I have no reason not to give it my all...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...for your sake, and for my own.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I'm sorry. I probably said too much... I hope I didn't make you uncomfortable.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Ah... Why isn't there a god yelling in the distance...
rows.speaker: Aidonian Spirit of the Dead

rows.text: "Indeed, my downtrodden fellow... Your sorrow and joy are but means for me to amuse myself."
rows.speaker: Aidonian Spirit of the Dead

rows.text: I will at least derive some comfort... If all the tears that I had shed were determined by some mightier being above.
rows.speaker: Aidonian Spirit of the Dead

rows.text: It's... you people...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Shut up... Just shut up!
rows.speaker: Styxian Spirit of the Dead

rows.text: Even if that girl is evil, there's no reason for you to absolve that monster.
rows.speaker: Styxian Spirit of the Dead

rows.text: It was the both of them... The both of them who trapped us in this crevice between life and death!
rows.speaker: Styxian Spirit of the Dead

rows.text: D—D—Don't be scared. They haven't noticed us at all.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: If Dan Heng was around, he'd definitely be able to raise the waters of the River of Souls into the sky...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: If Lady Hysilens was still alive, I think she might be able to do that, too.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The path ahead is blocked by the River of Souls again...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: In that case, let us go back to "the past"! This miracle sure is handy...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...This is yet another aspect of a Titan's divine power.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: We can't get through here. Let us return to "the present."
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: You seem to be able to discern both the past and the future...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Mem did it...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The pink squirrel... is very smart.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Why am I a squirrel now?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: The miracle's range is limited. Please come a little closer...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Heehee. Aren't I a good fit for {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s priest?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Of course, you're the most competent priest ever.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The alchemical matrix... should be behind this door.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Is that...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Don't look back... Keep moving forward, always.
rows.speaker: Eulogistic Butterfly

rows.text: It's yet another Eulogistic Butterfly... Are we getting closer to the nether realm?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Formation!
rows.speaker: Soldier B

rows.text: There are wandering souls of the deceased here as well...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: We must first return to "the present" before we can communicate with them.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Huh... So this path actually didn't exist back then?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s miracle has appeared...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Amazing! It's like we're inside a giant bubble. Even the river got parted.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: W—Wait! What if the miracle suddenly loses its effect?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Mem... Do you really want me to answer that?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Look. There's even a platform lift over there.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Go back whence you came... Go back...
Ahead lies the realm of the dead...
Don't be afraid, [Trailblazer]. Let's open our eyes wide... together!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Strange... For reflections in the River of Souls, they seem oddly... animated.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: These shadowy figures... are they illusions reflected by the River of Souls?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Hey, over here!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Could these dead monsters actually be...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: If Lady Cipher is to be believed... this could be the handiwork of Lord Mydei.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: He's still fighting against the black tide, even in the nether realm...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Someone's coming, ready...
rows.speaker: Soldier A

rows.text: Look! Pink puppies do exist!
rows.speaker: Soldier C

rows.text: This place... must have been a beautiful courtyard in the past.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: But how should we get up there?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The path is blocked yet again.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s aid always appears in times like this. How convenient...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: A "Chest of the Past" has been left behind, but none of its treasures remain inside...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: (I'm crying!)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Stay back... Don't come any closer!
rows.speaker: Ghost Voice

rows.text: This is his...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Living ones?
rows.speaker: Alchemist

rows.text: *A rumble from the distance*
This... This is...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Being cute isn't my only forte. I'm strong, too!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Um... I don't think I even meet the height requirement for the ticket, so I won't need one, right?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: This is Styxia, the city of dragons and waves... Anaxa hypothesizes that the missing {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} is somewhere in these ruins.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Anaxa had used a secret alchemical art to temporarily fuse his soul with {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#} and {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}. And when he was on the verge of death, he was pulled by {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} and caught a glimpse of the flowing River of Souls.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I have no idea. This circumstance... is completely unprecedented.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Why are you identifying as a dead person now? Don't give up on yourself!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Could it be that... You are the living being that those souls met...?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Umm... I still belong to the land of the living as of now, thank you very much!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Don't worry. It's time for me to shine...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Since the realm of the dead must remain peaceful, it's imperative that we rid the place of such discordant noise.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: What...?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: A campaign? Who are you campaigning against?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It's the same lines... Looks like he's still trapped in the moments before his death.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Indeed. While my relationship with the Council has always been quite ambiguous, Lady Aglaea has never taken any precautions against me. Instead... She's shown me nothing but complete trust.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I... really want to repay her for that trust.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I have seen too many farewells... Her distress is quite commonplace. There are those who will end their lives over what seems to be the smallest of worries.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This is a wish that I've held for almost a millennium. My mind might have changed once upon a time if people managed to strike up a friendship with me...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That's fine and all, but we need to lay down some rules. We're not gonna return to the past to steal things.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Broken stairs, blocked paths... This place is gonna fall down soon...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Do we need to enter that doorway to climb even higher? There seems to be a person... more like a soul guarding it.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: There's no need to be alarmed. We're just passing by the area. See? None of us look threatening.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You have? Then that's good.
rows.speaker: Alchemist

rows.text: You don't have to describe it like that, {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer]...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This is my guess...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Lord Mydei... You've been through some tough battles once again.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It seems like he's completely focused on resisting the temptation of the deads' whispers... He's working hard every minute to deny death.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I'm familiar... with this kind of mechanism.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Please calm down. If you were to fall into the icy cold River of Souls... I'm afraid that you really would die here.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Ugh... If I was more powerful, I would be able to carry one person with each limb and fly the four of us to the other side.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: It's still up to me to step up in a crisis... Wait here. I'll go check things out!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: That sounds so weird... Forget it. Just leave it to me!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Got it. Just leave it to me!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Heh...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: G—Get what? I'm getting even more confused...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Ah, I heard them too! So, what are those?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: No, not from me. The sounds that come from the memories when we were collecting the souls.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Trianne says yes! Trianne likes Little Cas and would love to take a picture with Little Cas!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: I have broken free from the chains of death countless times... This time will be no different.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I seek not to enter the door of the nether realm.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Castorice... Will you fulfill your duty for the Flame-Chase?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: They may look scary, but as long... as... we...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Are you...?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That's not funny!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: It's a deal then.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Are you feeling alright?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: She's the demigod of Trickery. When she flips the Coin of Whimsy into the air, she gains incredible speed that lets her travel anywhere in an instant.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Just like how she clearly had no intention of lingering here for even a second longer. We can only depend on ourselves for the rest of the way.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Don't worry. Mem's here to help!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: This is the land of their birth... Or perhaps of their death.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This alchemy, considered a sacrilegious act, might actually make the souls of mortals and Titans attract each other...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Even though {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} has been missing for a thousand years and even their followers haven't been able to find them... perhaps that special attraction could summon them here.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Oh! So are we going to use that Philosopher's Stone to... conjure the Titan?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I guess that's the only way. The only leads we have now are the name of this city and the fairy tale about the dragon...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} is even more mysterious than I am...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Indeed. Even one as erudite as Anaxa could only point us to this place, and no further. We will be entering the unknown as soon as we take our first steps... But that won't be the first time in my long journeys.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I believe that...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Rather than standing still, taking action is by far the better option. Perhaps fate might take pity on us today and show some compassion.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: What a beautiful butterfly. Is it talking to us?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: This is a Eulogistic Butterfly. They are found in places where many have met their demise.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: In Aidonia, some think of them as manifestations of {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}' benevolence. By turning the lingering obsessions of the deceased into these creatures, it is as if the Titan has made life into a specimen.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Others think of them as {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}' messengers that guide the departed to the nether realm.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The second theory sounds more believable. After all, the things they're saying are rather... um, direct?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Perhaps. But the fact that we're able to hear their whispers proves that we're fast approaching the realm of the dead.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But master... Did that lady really lie to us?
rows.speaker: Apprentice

rows.text: The centurion personally instructed us to inlay the inscription into his shield.
rows.speaker: Apprentice

rows.text: But now she's taken it away...
rows.speaker: Apprentice

rows.text: My child... that shield can never be cast, and there's no need for it anymore...
rows.speaker: Blacksmith

rows.text: Come, child, what is the name of that centurion again? Actually... Never mind, forget I said that.
rows.speaker: Blacksmith

rows.text: I'll wait with you for her to come back. When that happens, you'll be able to keep making shields.
rows.speaker: Blacksmith

rows.text: Mommy told us to go ahead first, but she's still not here yet.
rows.speaker: Young Girl

rows.text: One, two, three... I don't even know how many days have passed since then.
rows.speaker: Young Boy

rows.text: Perhaps Mommy will be back once you finish counting the days on all ten fingers.
rows.speaker: Young Girl

rows.text: One, two, three... It's been much longer than ten days since we left Mommy.
rows.speaker: Young Boy

rows.text: Do you... want to buy any fish?
rows.speaker: Marketplace Merchant

rows.text: Huh? He can see us?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Wait... More living people?
rows.speaker: Marketplace Merchant

rows.text: I'm not selling my fish to... living people. You lot are too... shameless. Buying fish without paying... If I ever see her again, I will... I will...
rows.speaker: Marketplace Merchant

rows.text: Could it be that... You're all dead souls that never achieved rest?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The nether realm... Does not exist...
rows.speaker: Marketplace Merchant

rows.text: Titan... Rejects... You... Me...
rows.speaker: Marketplace Merchant

rows.text: So... do you want to buy any fish?
rows.speaker: Marketplace Merchant

rows.text: But there aren't any "fish" nearby...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Are the fish... gone? The people... are gone, too...
rows.speaker: Marketplace Merchant

rows.text: I can only... keep selling fish. So... do you... want to buy any fish?
rows.speaker: Marketplace Merchant

rows.text: Apologies, I don't have much in the way of savings, but perhaps there's another way for me to release you from your suffering.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please relax. May you fall asleep peacefully... amid a gentle field of flowers.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This... this...
rows.speaker: Marketplace Merchant

rows.text: I knew it. These people aren't illusions. They're the souls of the deceased.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: They're supposed to reach the end of the west wind by floating down the River of Souls... Yet they have floundered upon the shoals of the stream, unable to move forward.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Did {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} reject them? Or perhaps they didn't really die at all?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Hang on...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Didn't he say... "more living people"? So that means he's seen other members of the living apart from us?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Could it be that these souls are stuck here due to someone's deceit?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: If something is done out of goodwill, are you really gonna call it "deceit"?
Goodwill? I can't see anything good out of—
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Wait a minute... Lady Cipher?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That's me.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: I couldn't take their behavior anymore, so I stole some things here and made up some lies there... Just trying to give them something to look forward to, you know?
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: ...It's because of vile living creatures like you that we're being misunderstood by all of them!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: What else am I supposed do? You can see the mess this place is in — These poor souls are denied by the nether realm, so now they're stuck in a few brief moments of their life, unable to move forward or back.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Did you see those two blacksmiths on the way? They've been here for as long as the sun's been around, wailing over and over about casting a shield... Styxia is so freaky.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Then why have you come back, Lady Cipher?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Hey, I'm not here to aid your adventure. I hate water more than anything else in this world, especially that stinky River of Souls...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: But... I just discovered some stuff before I left, and I reckon you should know about it.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: It's about that boy who defied death... I found traces of him here.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Lord Mydei...?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Oh right! That's his name! Well, now you know. As for whether that info is actually useful, that's for you lot to figure out.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: ...So long, Princess Homebody! So long, Gray Mystery!
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Huh? She disappeared just like that?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Lady Cipher has always been a... free spirit. In any case, she has brought us some valuable information.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: If Lord Mydei is also somewhere along the river shoals right now, then he will certainly become our signpost. After all, he's different from those wandering souls... He will find his way even in the realm of the dead.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s Rune of Recollection is nearby. Use prayers to return the river to before it got flooded!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Ah! Why are the black tide monsters here too? Can they swim in the River of Souls?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Even {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} wouldn't be able to accept black tide monsters into their realm...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: These traces seem to suggest that anybody who trespasses upon "Death"... will pay a heavy price.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please stay back... Let me deal with these enemies.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Ah, by the looks of it... you must be the foreign warriors that the queen had mentioned, right?
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: Since the current campaign requires the utmost care, I wasn't able to make time to welcome all of you. Please, forgive me.
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: ...Foreign warriors?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: A priestess, a warrior, and a, um... a divine beast... You look identical to the blessed saviors that the queen described!
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: Nobody knows... as of now.
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: Of the scouts that went ahead, only one has managed to return. He says that the land ahead is a forbidden land that should not be approached, as it's the doorway between the netherworld and the mortal realm...
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: As for the rest of the scouts... They've completely lost their souls and are decaying by the day.
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: While there is still dissension within the city, the scholars agree that this calamity was so unprecedented that it needed to be given a new designation.
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: An unprecedented calamity? Could it be... "Death"?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It seems that you have indeed heard about this. Well... "Death" is just one of the possibilities. It's too early to come to a definitive conclusion.
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: A world that has never seen "Death"... Looks like these people lived in the Era Chrysea, before the Calamity Titans descended upon the land.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: May I ask... where is the scout who managed to came back?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Though he returned to Styxia... he only had enough left in him to last no more than half a day. However, it was his intel that convinced us to rally together.
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: He said that he witnessed the demonic specter of an evil dragon at that treacherous land. The apparition opened its giant maw and devoured everything in sight, and thus brought Styxia that thing called "Death."
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: Styxia... an evil dragon that brings Death...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It all sounds rather familiar... Wait, wasn't this part of that fable?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Sir, could I... ask how the queen and princess are doing?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The queen?
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: — Ah, by the looks of it... you must be the foreign warriors that the queen had mentioned, right?
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: ...Leave it to me.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Sir, the war ended long ago. Styxia... no longer exists.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Styxia... is no more?
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: Th—This cannot stand! Newcomers, hurry up and go take your positions!
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: Looks like it's difficult for this gentleman to accept reality.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Sir, I am the Maiden of War sent here by the queen herself. If you accept my blessing, then today's battle will be smooth sailing.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Maiden of War? I've never heard of this... There's little time to waste. Please don't take too long.
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: Don't worry. I'm typically... unwilling to prolong such a moment.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Is it over...? Have we... won?
rows.speaker: Centurion

rows.text: Cas... Are you all right?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I—I'm fine. I just didn't expect that I would still have to "embalm" others even in the realm of the dead...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Is this... a remnant of his soul?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please excuse me. I am but a scholar from a distant land who had the misfortune of falling into the River of Souls and turned into a member of the dead...
rows.speaker: Court Scholar

rows.text: Huh? This one... seems to know that she's already dead.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Oh, I was merely speculating. But it seems I was right.
rows.speaker: Court Scholar

rows.text: And you... You... I recognize you. You're the Holy Maiden of "Death" from Aidonia, right?
rows.speaker: Court Scholar

rows.text: I'm sorry... I cannot bring you back to life. However, should you desire it, I can end your prolonged limbo.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Hah, I'm well aware of that. Even if you were able to revive me, I would never choose that option.
rows.speaker: Court Scholar

rows.text: That's because I didn't fall into the River of Souls by accident. Instead, I leaped into it to seek my death.
rows.speaker: Court Scholar

rows.text: ...Why?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: If you could see the life I've led, then you would not reproach me so. My life... was far too miserable.
rows.speaker: Court Scholar

rows.text: But I did not expect that things stay the same even in death! What a joke! In escaping my mortal life, I've entered a millennium of pain instead.
rows.speaker: Court Scholar

rows.text: Cerces above! What cowards humans are, for we fear both life and death simultaneously.
rows.speaker: Court Scholar

rows.text: I'm sorry... I'm also powerless to answer that question.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That's alright, Holy Maiden. At least you are able to respond to me. Please... grant me "Death."
rows.speaker: Court Scholar

rows.text: Cerces above... Does this count as thinking till the moment I die?
rows.speaker: Court Scholar

rows.text: For some people... This power that I possess is a "blessing" rather than a curse.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...But I never managed to convince myself of that.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Cas... Are you still trying to create a world without "Death"?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Yes. Because... When placed under time's vast scales, there is no worry in this world that cannot be solved.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But I've never been more firm in my conviction, now that I've learned about your near-death state — It is my duty to wipe "Death" from the face of this world.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Wow... This place is so spacious! Is this the kingdom's vault?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: D—Don't come near me...
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: Huh? Why does he look so panicked? Did the black tide monsters frighten him?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Or... is he actually scared of his own extraordinary power?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: You have a point, although...
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: While this might once have been the royal vault, it's since been plundered empty... So, please go away right this instant!
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: You've misunderstood us... We simply heard your shouts as we were passing by, then decided to come over to find out what happened.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: My goodness, did I really yell out loud? How rude of me...
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: I'm sorry to have bothered you. I merely saw a... warrior. While that spirit didn't harm me, his blows... really packed a hefty punch.
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: A warrior? Could it be...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Wait a minute. You seem to be quite different from him... Are you actually alive? How can you walk around here while alive?
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: It's a long story... We're here to seek an audience with {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}? Who's that?
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: Is it possible that... he's also living in the era before "Death" descended?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: "Death"... Could it be that you are here to defeat the evil dragon Pollux?
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: Pollux... Is that the embodiment of Thana — no, "Death"?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: According to the warriors under the centurion's command, that evil dragon has been dead for quite a while. The curse that condemns people to death didn't originate from it...
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: But they saw a girl within the dragon's embrace... And she is the true Reaper!
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: ...Pray tell, where is that girl right now?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I've heard that the queen spared no effort in bringing her back to the castle. Her Majesty intends to control all of Amphoreus with this unprecedented power...
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: As for whether this rumor is true... Well, no one knows.
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: You have my thanks for the invaluable insight that you've given us.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please treat this touch... as a token of my gratitude.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You... Are you...
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: Thank you...
rows.speaker: Vault Officer

rows.text: Oh... Could you be the scions of Styxia?
rows.speaker: Alchemist

rows.text: Did you hear about the great work that I'm doing here, and have thus arrived to give me the last material that I need for transmutation?
rows.speaker: Alchemist

rows.text: Great work?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Have you heard of the great name of Pollux, perchance?
rows.speaker: Alchemist

rows.text: During the age of myth, a time likely before your birth, I was the unsurpassed zenith of alchemy that none could reach! On the shoals of the River of Souls, I shall make Pollux soar again... and bring "Death" back to the world!
rows.speaker: Alchemist

rows.text: But... didn't that dragon already bring "Death" to the world?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Oh...? Looks like you don't know the whole picture.
rows.speaker: Alchemist

rows.text: While it's true that the missing girl can grant death to mortals... Pollux, the one who delivered her onto this world... Makes it so that humankind "cannot die."
rows.speaker: Alchemist

rows.text: So... It's just as I feared...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The deceased are supposed to drift down the River of Souls until they reach the end of the west winds, but this river of souls was blocked... by Pollux's fall.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That's right! That's why it's imperative that I bring the dragon back to the mortal realm and make it soar the skies again! I have long since prepared my alchemical matrix in the tower, although... I am still missing the most crucial material of all.
rows.speaker: Alchemist

rows.text: That final ingredient... The final sacrifice... Is none other than the girl who lives out her days with death!
rows.speaker: Alchemist

rows.text: Huh? What's going on? You didn't touch him, did you...?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I know that I am no longer capable of carrying out that task. Take this, all of you, and please, fulfill that great undertaking on my behalf...
rows.speaker: Alchemist

rows.text: This...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You...?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Lord Mydei...?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That black tide... is endless. My death... is only temporary.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I will find my path of return... and go back to the world of the living... and continue my "protection."
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Lord Mydei, I have always wanted to... Why does Death reject you?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I'm the one... resisting it. I must resist... the temptation to go with the flow...
rows.speaker: Mydei
