rows.text: I'll go against the current... and kill my way out of this cursed nether realm...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: That is... my destiny.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: It seems... his battlefield is not limited to the world of the living.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Lord Mydei, are you willing to travel with us?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: We're headed for the matrix inside that tower... to summon {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} from their prolonged concealment.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Tha... natos...{RUBY_E#}
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Challenge... death.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: That's right. If we can work together and defeat them... You won't have to be troubled by the curse of immortality any longer.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Let's go together, Castorice...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Let the person who has brushed against death countless times... guide your way...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Cas... Are you sure you want to do this? The alchemist said he wanted you to be a sacrifice...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: ...I'm not afraid. There's no reason for us to turn back anymore.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: "Rather than standing still, taking action is by far the better option. Perhaps fate might take pity on us today and show some compassion."
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Before you are rusted and broken chains, remnants of a path that once led to the tower.
...This is going to be difficult.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But I've never repaired... broken chains.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: The Rune of Recollection is here, but I can't find a Miracle Orb anywhere. So weird...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Could it be in that collapsed tower in the distance?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Wow, there are so many of you!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: It's Little Cas, and Little Gray! There's also... Little De and the pink puppy!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Trianne? Aren't you...
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: This is... the first time I've encountered a deceased friend while going upstream in the River of Souls.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: It really... works like this.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Just like the other departed spirits we've encountered along the way... I'm also unable to sense the aura of the living on Lady Trianne.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yup! You're right. Trianne already knows that she'll not be able to return to everyone's side.
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: But Trianne believed that Little Cas would eventually return to the nether realm...
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: So Trianne has been standing here, at this spot closest to the world of the living, and waiting for Little Cas!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: It must have been... very tough for you.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But according to what Trianne said... We're almost at the entrance of the nether realm.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Trianne promised Tribbie and Trinnon that when Little Cas got here, Trianne would get the gift ready and be the first person to run over and welcome you.
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: So, Little Cas, don't cry! Please accept this...
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: ...We finally finished it!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: This is what Lady Tribbie once mentioned...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The gift for me... that you didn't manage to finish...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The Holy Maiden of Janus... Even when separated by life and death, their thoughts are still connected.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Trianne spent a lot of time drawing this! Trianne hopes that Little Cas likes it.
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Mmm... Seriously...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It's seriously... A wonderful drawing, Lady Trianne...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This is... our "Flame-Chase Journey"...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Little Cas, we don't know what your journey was like before. Tribbie has always said that it must have been a very harsh and frightening journey.
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: But Little Cas no longer has anything to fear now, because everyone is here with you in this Flame-Chase Journey!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: That's right...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Only now, when I see Lady Trianne's gift, do I realize that I've already obtained so many things I would never have dared to dream of since I embarked on the Flame-Chase Journey.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It's the first time I've gained so many companions, the first time I picked up the hobbies of crafting and photography, the first time I had dinner with someone else, the first time I went to the market to buy the chimera doll I'd liked for a very long time and hugged it to sleep...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The first time I wore a dress personally made by Lady Aglaea... the first time I went for a walk with Lady Tribbie, Lady Trianne, and Lady Trinnon... the first time I enjoyed the night breeze and looked up at the stars with Miss Hyacine... the first time I took care of dromases with [Trailblazer]...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Looking back at all these experiences I never thought were possible... it feels as though the scales of my life had shrunk from centuries and decades down to minutes and seconds, and all of them are so precious...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I took countless photos in the past, but they're all black-and-white landscapes. I don't have a single one with friends.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: If I had known... I would have taken more pictures...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: "...And now, the objective is complete. That is all."
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Such is what Professor Anaxa always says after preparing for an alchemical ritual. And now —
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Pollux, I shall lift you from the River of Souls and reforge your soul. Perhaps you will be disturbed by this, and your body may become horrifying to behold...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But if even the slightest trace of your soul remains, the soul that once ferried me to this side of the shore, then please look at me. I wish to thank you in person — I have obtained everything you sacrificed your divinity for.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Lady Amunet...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Did she recognize you...? She must be the first soul we can communicate with here, right?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: I'm afraid she is just another spirit trapped here, like the rest of them. The only difference is that I was there when she died.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Please, go on. I'm listening. Are you about to tell the story of Styxia?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yes. You're just as smart as I imagined, but...
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: ...Nevermind. Now's not the time.
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: There's no need to worry, Elder. Take a look around you... You're already at the resting place of the dead.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The world of the dead? But how...
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: I understand that you chose to remain silent about the story to protect Castorice, the girl who coexists with death...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But you no longer need to hide that story. I can assure you that you have protected that girl's life well.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Well, in that case, let me begin.
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: Then... let the ritual begin.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Styxia, the pearl of the ocean, plagued by unwarranted calamity and ravaged by death in the fairy tale — It was the first city-state to shift their faith towards "Death," even before Aidonia did.
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: From where you stand now, I suppose that's a bit hard to believe, right?
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: Indeed... I cannot imagine that those from the Era Chrysea, blessed with eternal life, could ever yearn for death.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Heh... I have pondered the same question, child. But I'm afraid there is no clear answer to it.
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: "Journeys and epics are only glorious and magnificent because all things eventually fade to dust." That's how someone once explained to me why death is necessary to the world.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But I still can't take that as the final answer... Would a world without journeys and epics be worse off?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Heh... I take it the one who spoke this line was a general? Or perhaps a warrior?
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: I, however, did find some inspiration in these words. Would you like to hear my thoughts, Castorice?
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: Please enlighten me, Lady Amunet. Though I have already made up my mind on how to handle the authority and Coreflame of "Death"...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Your words might truly guide me toward the path forward.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You and I are neither warriors nor generals. Therefore, journeys and epics cannot truly resonate with us.
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: But what if I reframe it like this — what if "love" is not a trait bestowed upon mortals by Mnestia, but a blessing from death?
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: "Love"...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: No one ever invented the word "cherish" in the era when life was eternal, for all the good things in the world could be revisited endlessly, and every bond formed carried no risk of being severed.
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: The so-called Era Chrysea was an age devoid of both virtue and sin. People did not truly live — they simply existed, going through the motions without passion or purpose, then waiting for something to happen.
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: Perhaps the people of Styxia chose to embrace death not out of fascination with its cruel and fearsome side...
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: But instead became fixated and obsessed with the impulses and desires tied to a finite existence.
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: Therefore, "Death" is not a thing of fear and desperation, but...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That's right, Castorice. It is the reason we shed tears when parting ways... and also the original spark that ignited the passion of mortals.
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: If you truly intend to deprive the world of "Death," then be prepared to witness it return to a state of stagnation.
rows.speaker: Amunet

rows.text: I understand, Lady Amunet.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Our limited lifespan shapes all that we know and love... Not even the Death Titan has the right to take that away from humankind again.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: "Mnestia's Love" was the Chrysalis of Gold's first blessing, but it most likely wasn't understood by mankind. We only learned to interpret this wonderful gift after {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}' arrival.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: If the world was bereft of death, then the Queen of Styxia wouldn't have played midwife in delivering me into this world... You wouldn't have welcomed me into Aidonia... And Aglaea would never have invited me to join the Flame-Chase Journey. None of these stories would ever have happened.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: And I... Would never have lived, let alone found happiness.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Thank you, mother...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I will use all the "love" I've experienced in this long life to complete the final miracle.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Sadly...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Being departed souls, our images cannot be captured in the world of the living.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...I thought so, too.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: What? Are we seriously going to leave any room for regret?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: There won't be any regrets...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This vivid drawing surpasses any photograph from the world of the living.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Little Cas smiled! Tribbie, Trinnon, and Trianne's wish has finally come true.
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: I remember you once said that fate is not the flowers that bloom at the end of the road, but where people tread beyond the gate... Now, the path that belongs to me is about to reach the end.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Thank you... for bringing me the final key.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Key? Little Cas, why are you talking in riddles all of a sudden?
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: I have a feeling that soon, this gift of yours will become the key to saving {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} [Trailblazer]'s life.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Wow! That's amazing! Then keep smiling and carry on bravely!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Little Cas, Little Gray, everyone — see you tomorrow!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: With a blinding smile, Trianne's golden form disappears in the thin fog of Styxia's moonlit night.
Lady Trianne...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The aura of this place... We have indeed reached the end of the Stream of Souls.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: If I go any further... I might lose myself. I must leave now, for the black tide still wreaks havoc in the realm of the living.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I have yet to make my decision, Lord Mydei.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Heh...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: No matter... Make the choice your heart desires. Even if it takes a thousand years of waiting...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I will continue to fight till I die... Then rise from death... til the miracle descends.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: There is one more thing you should know, Lord Mydei.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...What is it?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Professor Anaxa may have deduced the principles behind the Era Nova. You and I... may be reincarnated as "Strife" and "Death" in the next cycle, becoming calamities wreaking havoc upon the world.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...I see.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: ...Is that all? Are you going to accept such a fate without complaints?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Do you have... a strategy to shatter the shackles of our fate?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: I... haven't found it yet. Perhaps I never will...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Then... cease wasting your thoughts on futile matters.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Control what little you can. And when fate's inescapable grasp comes...
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Resist it with the strength of your mighty will.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Thank you, Lord Mydei. I will find the right decision.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: In the name of "Strife"... may you meet a fitting end.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: This must be the alchemical matrix the spirit mentioned. Let's see... We need to insert "Aquila's Sky," "Georios's Earth," "Kephale's Fire," "Phagousa's Ocean"...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: And "Mnestia's Love"...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It seems our sweet Princess Homebody has made up her mind...
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: In that case, Seamstress, I suppose I no longer need to deliver your message — my time is rather precious, after all.
rows.speaker: Cipher

rows.text: Whether you wish to break free from death or not, please follow your heart. By the promise you once made, I ask that you fulfill your duty one final time —
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Castorice, please live as a human... And die as one.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I'm sorry I have to wake you up from ancient death...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: And I know you're anxious... Shh, don't be afraid...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Do you remember me? I'm the girl you once carried across the Sea of Souls.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I'm sorry I wasn't able to remember you, but with the help of many people, I was finally able to pick up these broken fragments of my past...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...I'm back, Pollux.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I know this might not be what you wanted.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But I have to do this.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: So please, carry me across the Sea of Souls again and return me to the nether realm, just like you did in the past...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please take me to where the Coreflame of "Death" rests.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...I'll be going now.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: (What's... happening...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Huh...? What's wrong...!?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: What's wrong with {M#him?}{F#her?}
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: {M#His}{F#Her} time is almost up. If I don't go now, I'm afraid {M#his}{F#her} soul will return to {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}' embrace before me.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: What! Oh no... Is there anything we can do?
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Don't worry. I promised I would ask {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} for the Trailblazer's right to roam the earth again.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Mem, stay here and keep a close watch until I return, alright?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Alright! I'm the best at taking care of others.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Go on, Cas. Make sure not to leave yourself with any regrets.
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Please...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Wait for me.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Lord Anaxa, you're finally here!
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: The last speaker for the assembly will be taking the stage soon. The resolution will be passed after that.
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: Lady Caenis has reserved a special seat for you. Shall I show you to it?
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: Lead the way.
Not now.
Alright. This way, please.
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: As you command.
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: Lady Caenis has reserved a special seat for you. Shall I show you to it?
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: Lead the way.
Not now.
Alright. This way, please.
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: As you command.
rows.speaker: Military Runner

rows.text: The last vote...
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: Who will he vote for?
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: Hmph, always the performer.
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: Talk about a grand entrance...
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: Vote for Caenis!
rows.speaker: Adult male

rows.text: The die is cast...
rows.speaker: Adult female

rows.text: Phainon... So, they are leaving the final debate to him.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heh...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I trust you haven't forgotten the world we've envisioned together.
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: At the same time, in Okhema
*Loud cheers from afar*
Time flies... In the blink of an eye, the fifteenth {RUBY_B#dawn}Entry Hour{RUBY_E#} is already at hand.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: When this farce is over, your soul will be placed on the scales of life and death. Are you ready?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: No need to ask so many times — of course I am.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Then why do you drag your feet? Is your fear of crowds holding you back again?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hmph, I simply find them too noisy. Paying attention to conceited fools like them would be an utter waste of my time.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Such harsh words. As I see it, you are no less arrogant than they are.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I couldn't agree more.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh? I did not expect to hear that from you. Are you not going to refute me?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I know myself better than you think I do... At the very least, better than a stowaway like you.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: And they say men whose ends are nigh have but kind words.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Well that is exactly why I chose you.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hmph, should I thank you for the compliment?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The hour of the trial has come. Do you have an answer for me? And... how will you prove the veracity of your argument?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I suppose there is no point in putting this off any longer. Do you recall where we stopped the last time?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You were saying that Amphoreus' history is cyclical...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Indeed. The demigods that bear the Coreflames eventually become the new Titans at the world's end...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Remember what happened on the holy mountain? Calypso, Gnaeus... As their destined ends approached, one by one, they left this world... leaving only the twins, who were fated to succeed Death.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Unfortunately, while their journey is consistent with ours — you and Calypso as well as Nikador and Gnaeus act as supporting evidence — I can only come up with a rough sketch for my theory of a cyclical history.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: For all the pains I took to reach this point, I had already lost hope of ever obtaining definitive proof. After all, the past is in the past. Proving that we are the legacies of heroes of the past is a hopeless endeavor.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: That is, until I met a girl named Polyxia and her sister.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: If Castorice was truly sent from the past to the present for the Titan's self-serving reasons, then having lived through two cycles and with Styxia as the pivot, she will no doubt be the link to connect all of this together.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: If the twins of Death can bridge two cycles to reunite at the shores of the Sea of Souls... then my hypothesis will no longer be just a hypothesis, and you, too, will get the answer to your question.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: That is all well and good, but how can you be so sure? If there is even the slightest error in your hypothesis, the girl will be shattered.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hmph, it matters not. The most important quality a scholar must possess is foolhardiness. If you are overly cautious, then you'll never have the gumption to make the first step, and change will never come.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Besides, I, Anaxagoras, am destined to overturn this farcical world.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Come, let us go and teach those pathetic worms one final lesson.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Let those Chrysos Heirs who started this terrible war hear you!
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Let them hear the voices of the people!
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: *fanatic cheering*
As always, that woman knows how to stir up a crowd.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Professor Anaxa...? I thought you'd pass on this.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Everyone must cast their vote, or this assembly would serve no purpose.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Prof... Do you truly think it's wise to entrust the fate of the world to an assembly like this?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Okhema has stood strong under this system for a thousand years. It stands to reason that there is purpose in its existence.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But that is not what you're asking, is it? What you really want to know is: Is Aglaea making the right decision in entrusting the fate of the world to you?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...Nothing ever escapes you.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I didn't spend all those years teaching you for nothing. Most people only take four years to graduate, if I recall.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Haha... To tell the truth, I feel like I'm on my way to an execution chamber instead of a podium.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: So... do you have an answer to that question?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: No, I don't.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I thought so...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Because that question is not yours to ask in the first place.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Is "Aglaea entrusting the world to you" the right decision? Don't make me laugh. That is a question that woman must answer herself. Why are you fretting about this on her behalf? Or have you been seeing yourself as her pawn all this time?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Listen up, I'll say this only once. Flip your perspective around and ask yourself this instead, "What should I do to ensure that the world doesn't stray from the correct path?" That is what you should be thinking about.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You still have time, so give it some thought. Oh, and don't bother telling me the answer.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Tell it to those begging for salvation from the gods.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Got it.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Thank you, Professor Anaxa.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That's Anaxagoras to you.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Who... who'll you be voting for?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That'll depend on how well you perform... May Cerces safeguard your thoughts.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: *crowd chatter*
Elders and citizens, silence, if you please. As the Theoros, I present to you:
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Phainon of Aedes Elysiae, virtuous citizen of Okhema and the last speaker of the assembly.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Much obliged, Lord Lygus.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I remember him — he's the penniless lad working for Aglaea!
rows.speaker: Arrogant Citizen

rows.text: Where's Lady Goldweaver? Why is she sending this guy to give the last speech? Is this really the end of the Flame-Chase Journey?
rows.speaker: Confused Citizen

rows.text: Can this dude really face down Caenis...?
rows.speaker: Calm Citizen

rows.text: *crowd chatter*
By Kephale above, dear citizens of Okhema...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: As you look upon me, so too do I see you.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I see your fear and misgivings, your apprehension about the discord between the Chrysos Heirs and the Council of Elders... and your uneasiness about the future of the holy city.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Yet, before you contemplate something as grand as the fate of the world, I ask that you look closer... Look, beyond the horizon illuminated by {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}, at the crisis threatening to overwhelm us!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What...?
rows.speaker: Calm Citizen

rows.text: Aedes Elysiae, my beloved hometown, is a village forgotten by time. It is a place with the most invigorating breeze and wheat fields that spread all the way to the sea... I once thought that there, I would enjoy a lifetime of peace and quiet with my friends and family.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: How I wish I could invite all of you to that paradise far away from the noise and chatter of the world! Alas, I can't...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...Because she... and all that she nurtured... all that I loved... they have long been devoured by the black tide. My beloved home... is no more.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: In an uproar, representative leaders from different cities in Okhema throw pieces of pottery into the dolium...
At the present time, on the scales of {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#}, those who call for the continuation of the Flame-Chase Journey and those who demand its suspension...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Each faction holds an equal share of the votes, resulting in the perfect balance.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: As expected, this is the moment when the Flame-Chase Journey is the closest to its end.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: And now, it's your turn to vote, Lord Anaxagoras.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Is there anyone else who hasn't voted?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: No, you're the last. Cast your vote with care, for your decision will break this impasse.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: I have long since made a decision.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Very well. May you bring much-needed change to this farcical world.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You... you are...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Well done, child. Just as I foresaw, you have achieved great things.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Teacher...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What a twist of fate... A blasphemer raised in the doctrines of the Venerationists. It's like a foal kicking its mother in the belly after taking all her milk.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: I respect you immensely, sir, but—
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You cherish the truth even more.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: So, child, do not be troubled by the criticisms I have borne. Do not let those voices hinder you as you forge ahead.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: As the Sage of the Venerationists, I am duty-bound to oppose you. But as your friend and mentor, Anaxagoras, I say:
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: Go forth, for the truth is already in your hands.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: ...I will keep that in mind.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Go now, child. Your lonely pursuit is about to welcome a new chapter...
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: And when you reach the end of this journey, may we meet again with the truth before us.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: You have my word, sir. May Cerces safeguard your thoughts.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: May Cerces safeguard your thoughts.
rows.speaker: Empedocles

rows.text: You are right, Empedocles. My lonely pursuit is about to welcome a new chapter. I must be on my way now...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: May we meet again with the truth before us, Empedocles.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What are you waiting for? Just cast your vote—
rows.speaker: Dramatic Citizen

rows.text: Silence! Silence, everyone!
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Behold, {RUBY_B#Reason Titan}Cerces{RUBY_E#}. Here at the center of the world, I shall write the final step of my proof...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: For this place is but one step away from the truth.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: With the balance shattered, the result is clear. By {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} and {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#} above, as the Theoros, I have observed...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: No! Lygus, you can't...!
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Anaxa! What have you done!? Have you lost your mind!?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: I hope you are prepared for the harsh punishment awaiting you! Mark my words, I will make sure that clever head of yours never forgets the price of betrayal!
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Have you forgotten? I told you, that happens to be one of my rare talents.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You put on such a grand performance... just to aid their preposterous Flame-Chase Journey!?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Performance? No, you are quite mistaken. I may be paranoid by nature, but I've always been known for my honesty.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: If you really understood me, Lady Caenis, you'd realize that I never had any interest in your pathetic little game of politics. Factions, standpoints... they are jokes in my eyes. I have never once switched sides...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Because I, and I alone, am the truth.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Lady Caenis, with all the citizens here as witnesses, we should honor the spirit of democracy and respect the decision of this assembly.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: ...I have observed that Okhema has chosen her destiny! This citizens' assembly has resolved to continue the Flame-Chase Journey. This resolution shall be put up on the Wall of Heroes such that all citizens are aware of the city's way forward.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You...!
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: It seems not everyone is ready for the assembly to end. Very well, let me entertain you for a little longer.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: By your leave, Lord Lygus.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Interesting...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Elders and citizens, your attention, please! Stay for a moment more, if you will. Anaxagoras of the Grove of Epiphany has an announcement for the assembly.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: *crowd chatter*
Just moments ago, all of you made a decision on the fate of Amphoreus. As a supporter of the Flame-Chase Journey, it pleases me to see the choice you have made.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But I regret to say that I still harbor doubts about this outcome. Thus, I hereby challenge this resolution!
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Huh...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Tell me, who among you dares swear on {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}'s name that Era Nova will truly welcome the fairy-tale ending that the Chrysos Heirs have promised? A beautiful new world free of calamity and madness?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: *crowd chatter*
No one? Must I pick somebody to answer?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Very well. You, the one acting so wise and profound — in front of all present here, do you dare swear that it will happen for sure?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: No? Fine, next. You, the one with ignorance written all over your face... Yes, you. Do you dare swear by it in front of the Titan?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What are you trying to do?
rows.speaker: Confused Citizen

rows.text: Hmph, useless! Your turn, then. With that smug look of yours, you must be confident that the Flame-Chase Journey is the best course to take, right?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Hey! Mind your tongue!
rows.speaker: Arrogant Citizen

rows.text: So, no one? I see. In that case, Phainon, answer me this: Your speech was filled with such passion just now. How confident, then, are you in making this promise?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: *crowd chatter*
Elders and citizens, silence, if you please!
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Anaxagoras of the Grove of Epiphany has made his statement clear. As per Okhema's Codex, I request all present citizens to stand with me in exercising the right of judgment.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: First, Elder Caenis of Okhema and Lygus the Theoros stand accused of neglecting their duties and abusing the law, leading to the egregious blasphemy against a god...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: In the names of {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#} and {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}, Okhema is to form a committee before the seventh {RUBY_B#Noon}Action Hour{RUBY_E#} to conduct an investigation and disclose the findings to the public for subsequent judgment!
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Agreed! Agreed!
rows.speaker: Citizens' Assembly

rows.text: Curse you...!
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Now, concerning Anaxagoras of the Grove of Epiphany, he has confessed to grave blasphemy against {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: In the names of {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#} and {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}, the accused must be allowed to hear the "people's voice" prior to the execution for a chance at a reduced sentence and possible pardon!
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Let him die! Let him die!
rows.speaker: Citizens' Assembly

rows.text: Professor...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Let him die! Let him die!
rows.speaker: Citizens' Assembly

rows.text: Let him die! Let him die!
rows.speaker: Citizens' Assembly

rows.text: Let him die! Let him die!
rows.speaker: Citizens' Assembly

rows.text: Let him die! Let him die!
rows.speaker: Citizens' Assembly

rows.text: What decision will you make, Lady Goldweaver?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Enough with the hesitation, Aglaea. This is not like you.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Let him die! Let him die! Let him die! Let him die!
rows.speaker: Citizens' Assembly

rows.text: Then, in light of the "people's voice"...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: O {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#} on high, may you bring death upon him.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: *fanatic cheering*

I will never forget the day the black tide struck. My father, Hieronymus, fought with a broken sword to his last breath to protect his child. My mother, Audata... She was ripped apart by monsters, all so I might live to stand before you here and now.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Galba... He was a hunter. But in the end, those arms that once drew a bow instead embraced Piso, his beloved son, as they both breathed their last. Pythias, the teacher, risked her life to save her students, but a burning beam fell on her, crushing her...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: And what of Livia, her daughter? Did she make it out alive? ...No, she didn't. Livia, Piso, and so many other children... My childhood friends... They were all swallowed by the black tide and turned into monsters.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: They kept saying the same thing over and over... even up until the final moment I finally steeled my heart and granted them eternal peace with my sword:
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: "Why, Phainon? Aren't we the best of friends?"
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That is the black tide — a looming threat that can bring Okhema to its knees anytime. Caenis may have promised that, with the Three Titans of Calamity gone, Okhema will return to an Era Chrysea once more, but...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Much as it pains me, I must disappoint you: While {RUBY_B#Mydei}the demigod of Strife{RUBY_E#} has done everything in his power to hold them back, "they" are still coming.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: By now, the name of that black-robed swordmaster... the Flame Reaver, has likely echoed throughout the city already. The roaring thunder is a message from the Strife demigod: The Flame Reaver has risen from death, and they hunger for the Coreflames of the gods.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Lies! If such a powerful enemy is indeed approaching, why is Okhema still a picture of peace?
rows.speaker: Arrogant Citizen

rows.text: Exactly! The city of Okhema shows no signs of pandemonium or chaos. And why is that? I beg you, spare a moment to think about this. Are we able to stand here and hold this assembly in peace today because the danger has passed?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: No! This peace we enjoy is no gift of fate. We are able to stand here today only because the Chrysos Heirs have stepped up and shielded Okhema from calamity! With her golden threads, Aglaea has preserved — and continues to preserve — these idyllic days that all of you hold dear!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Heh...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The Council of Elders claims that Aglaea will one day forsake the people because her divinity is eroding her body and soul. But ask yourselves this: Rather than offering her aid and support, why do they choose to watch and push Okhema away from the Flame-Chase Journey?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The answer that no one can bring themselves to speak of... A truth stained in blood and buried in greed, fear, and vanity... Allow me to lay it bare before you.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: It is because the Council of Elders, which bears Okhema's history and honor, along with this citizens' assembly we once took so much pride in, are now infested with vermin!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: You insolent whelp! How dare you—
rows.speaker: Angry Citizen

rows.text: It is true that Aglaea has reached her limit. Why? Because she has been working tirelessly to weave the defenses of our holy city against the encroaching evil — all while these vermin are making up baseless accusations about her and scheming in the shadows!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Not once has she ever failed Okhema, yet these vermin attempt to tear her apart, tarnishing her name with unfounded allegations! She may have been blessed by divinity, but hasn't her heart always stayed true to humanity?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: They attempt to mislead you and reduce this assembly to a crude standoff between gods and humans, but citizens of Okhema! Once more, I implore you to open your eyes and look at those around you!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Examine them closely! Beneath all that finery, do you see the good heart of a human... or the poisonous glands of a pest?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Make your judgment, then turn your gaze to the demigods whom so many of you regard as cold and merciless — do you not see the light of humanity in them? And those who wear the mask of humanity yet utter only hurtful, slanderous words — can you not see that their souls have been corrupted by power?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Yet, no matter what your answer is, and no matter who your vote goes to... rest assured that you have nothing to fear.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: For Aglaea, Tribios, and I will remain your faithful guardians and pledge our lives to upholding your decision.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: And this vow will stay true until the end of our days, where it will be passed on to future Flame-Chasers...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: ...A steadfast and unwavering promise that shall endure through the ages!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: *crowd chatter*
You've done well, Phainon. Given the circumstances, delivering a rousing speech to stir up emotions was a prudent move.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Thank you all for your patience. On behalf of the Seven Sages of the Grove of Epiphany and the scholars of Amphoreus, I, Anaxagoras, am ready to cast my vote.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But before that, in the interest of fairness, Lady Goldweaver, I pose a question to you before all who are gathered here:
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Will you, as Phainon has promised, stand by the decision made in the assembly, regardless of outcome?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: In the interest of fairness... I make no promises, lest it should influence your decision.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Heh, very well. I thank you for your honesty.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What's he doing?
rows.speaker: Confused Citizen

rows.text: The stakes are high. Let's be patient.
rows.speaker: Calm Citizen

rows.text: Cut the act! Who do you think you are, wasting our time like this?
rows.speaker: Arrogant Citizen

rows.text: Lord Anaxa, please do not forget that I—
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Rule number one: Do not call me Anaxa. Rule number two: Never interrupt me. Silence is golden.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: *crowd chatter*
Just vote already! What are you waiting for?
rows.speaker: Citizens' Assembly

rows.text: Cast... your... vote...
rows.speaker: Citizens' Assembly

rows.text: I cannot help but wonder: Is every hardship in the world something you will exploit and use to your advantage?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Heh, how else am I supposed to make use of this situation where my body and soul are separated?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: O Cerces — or should I say, Calypso — accompany me on this final journey.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Let us journey to the nether realm and see how she will substantiate the answer to your question and validate my decision.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: We need only to follow the sound of the tides...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Professor! What are you doing?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Let him continue with his performance.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Haha! Will you look at that? Even Phainon and Aglaea lack the courage to make such a promise!
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: And what's even more absurd is that no one but I can promise you this new world, and yet the assembly passed the resolution anyway!
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But you needn't worry because I knew better than to trust you good-for-nothings. That is precisely why I am here today — to give you one final lecture!
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Now, listen up, and listen well! I, Anaxagoras of the Grove of Epiphany, hereby declare:
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Everything that the Flame-Chase Journey promises is true! Phainon of Aedes Elysiae, the prophesized demigod who shall succeed {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}, will reforge each and every one of us in the new world with his complete, intact memories!
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What...?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: The Coreflame-bearing Titans were the Chrysos Heirs of yesterday, and the Chrysos Heirs who carry the Coreflames today will become the Titans of tomorrow.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: All of our souls shall endure for eternity in the miracle of the Worldbearer, and all under Kephale's protection shall step into that new world!
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: *crowd chatter*
What!? Are you saying that we must bow down to you and worship you even in our next lives!?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Enough, you blasphemous imbecile! How dare you try to deceive us with all these lies and falsehoods! How can you prove—
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: I told you, don't interrupt me! But since you've asked, I shall be kind and indulge you: My statements are based on my experiments on the divine body of {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#} themself!
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You heard me correctly, everyone! With the tacit approval of Caenis and the Council of Elders, I fused my soul with a god through alchemy and learned the truth behind Era Nova!
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What is he talking about...?
rows.speaker: Confused Citizen

rows.text: Isn't that pure blasphemy?
rows.speaker: Confused Citizen

rows.text: I, the vile, wretched blasphemer, deserve nothing less than death for my sins...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: And the Council of Elders, which granted me consent and aided me in committing this atrocity, should face punishment alongside me!
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: By the gods, even Caenis has betrayed Okhema...
rows.speaker: Dramatic Citizen

rows.text: *crowd chatter*
I—I had no knowledge of his transgressions...! He did that on his own! The Council of Elders bears no responsibility for his actions!
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Lord Lygus... As the esteemed Theoros, are you going to simply stand by and allow the Council of Elders to be dragged through the mud!?
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: If the accusation is true, I will acknowledge it. If not, my conscience stands unburdened. Lady Caenis, the reputation of the Council of Elders was not built in a day, nor will it be shattered overnight.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Repercussions await those who fool the people, and punishment must be meted out to those who abandon their vows. We should respect this beautiful city and her people.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You...
rows.speaker: Caenis

rows.text: Lady Aglaea, the Goldweaver, I humbly ask that you take on the responsibility of overseeing this judgment, in the name of the fairness of {RUBY_B#Law Titan}Talanton{RUBY_E#} and the justice of {RUBY_B#Worldbearing Titan}Kephale{RUBY_E#}...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: ...Considering the circumstances, and in accordance with Okhema's Codex, as the only demigod among us, you shall rightfully wield this authority.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: ...The honor is mine to bear.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I'm gladdened by your triumphant return...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Farewell, then. May we... reunite in the new world.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Don't stop, don't turn back, don't look down. Or up, for that matter.
rows.speaker: Acheron

rows.text: A number of thin sheets of ice have shackled the unconscious March 7th to her bed. The once warm bedroom is now permeated with a bitter cold.
The young girl lays silent and flawless in the ice... Just as she did back when she was drifting through space.
Curled up in the clear ice, the young girl remains silent with her eyes fixed shut.
Although the ice is not cold to the touch, there is something particularly saddening about seeing a young girl who is normally so full of life fall into complete silence.
May Cerces safeguard your thoughts.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Every departed soul who has arrived here has expressed the same.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You're still as energetic as always.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Did you know? Every flower here was planted by Thanatos themself. These flowers were originally both lifeless and immortal, but in the first rain brought by the River of Souls, they were given new life, flourishing as the bearers of countless souls...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Thank you.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Mm, just like the other demigods, I will stay here... and embrace my destiny.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Rest assured, "defying death" is {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}' divine authority. Fortunately, your soul hasn't dissipated. This is not a resurrection, but the extradition of a dying person back to the present world.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I am... glad to hear that.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: (What's this...!?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...Let the Trailblazing... continue.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...I agree.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: She might not have been able to change her fate, but she still wrote the final verse of her epic herself.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: O! Gods who have returned, and gods who are still watching! Today, we bring you a soul laid bare.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: (I'm... back.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: At last... I knew you could do it.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Your soul is still perfectly whole, as if some kind of force is trying its best to keep it together.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Is it {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#}'s final blessing? Or... is it a miracle of your own?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It's truly... incredible. Such a strange surge of familiarity... so hard to describe.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Perhaps it is fate, once again fulfilling its own design. Or perhaps it is the laws from beyond the sky, so familiar to you, [Trailblazer], that intertwined our {RUBY_B#Paths}fates{RUBY_E#} long ago...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...It seems that this is a riddle which cannot be solved anytime soon.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The sensation of becoming a demigod is truly wondrous. It's as if the River of Souls is winding its way through the depths of my spirit, transforming with each breath into a fine rain that nourishes the world...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Do you recall that prophecy? "At the end of the sea of flowers, the souls of the living shall warm thy fingertips, and after an embrace... there shall be eternal separation."
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I promised you that I would do everything in my power to give it another meaning. Now, as I stand as a demigod and destiny draws to a close...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I can finally end it in a way that is as beautiful as it deserves.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The wish I once sought but could never grasp is now within reach. In this brand-new world, every blooming life will lift its arms in celebration, and recount the profound meaning of this very instant...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Every touch, every embrace we share, will never again be an ice-cold loss...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: They will radiate with an intense warmth, sowing love far and wide throughout the land.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Presently, in Okhema
That grand and absurd performance was what you've been seeking your whole life?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I gave up everything in search of truth, and it culminated in this very moment.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You, on the other hand, performed as I expected. You did not hesitate when you saw the chance to attain power. It's as if you...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...Crave power like a fly craves rot.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Those are your words, not mine.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But what you said at the end... Did you already know what I had planned for Phainon?
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I may have lost an eye, but my vision is clearer than anyone else. You've nearly exhausted your humanity. You're no different from my current state as a walking corpse.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: That's true. I've long since burned to ash over the past one thousand years. Only he is capable of unleashing a raging fire that rivals our final great enemy — {RUBY_B#Sky Titan}Aquila{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: So, this is our last chance. How about we let go of the bad blood between us?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: May I resonate with your Coreflame, Aglaea?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Please do.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: That's... impossible. To persist with your soul thinned to such an extent... You're insane.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Just as you fight to lug your corpse onward to complete your unfinished goals, I have my own reasons for doing this.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Until Phainon grows into his position as the prophesied leader, I must continue to lead everyone on the Flame-Chase Journey. I must keep inching forward, even if only as an empty shell.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: I've long predicted this was the case, but I didn't think you'd already lost so much.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heh, how ironic. We would have avoided so many misunderstandings if you and I had just spoken this candidly before.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But casting aside our ideological differences, there is one thing you and I agree on.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Phainon.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Yes. He was born to be a hero. He understands the hearts of the people, and I can confidently say he is a far better leader than you. Only he is capable of fulfilling your mission.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...Sadly, he is a man cursed by {RUBY_B#Romance Titan}Mnestia{RUBY_E#}. But by my estimates, his horribly elaborate sense of style should not impede Era Nova.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Congratulations are in order. We've found common ground at the very end of our destined paths.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: When you put it that way, it makes me want to take back what I said.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Aglaea! We're back!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Come welcome [Trailblazer], our great hero reborn from the ashes.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I hope he didn't hear your earlier assessment.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Hmph, it wouldn't be the first time I criticized him. A man should be aware of his own shortcomings.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Heh, she made quite a scene. I suppose it's my turn now.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I won't stop you...
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Professor, you...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: What's with that look? You were present.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: So, let's get this execution over with. We wouldn't want to bring shame to Okhema's divine laws or keep me from creating a new world.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: You never change, do you, Professor?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: I don't understand. If your theory is correct, you'll lose all memories of your past life once you become a Titan, so what's the point of becoming a god?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Of course there's a point. Even if I forget who I am, I'll still have my brilliant mind.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: It goes without saying I'll find a way to retrieve memories of my past life. Besides, I still have you, don't I?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: I still don't really understand what you said during the assembly. Even if it were true, things reforged from memory could never be the same as the original anyway.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Then allow me to tell you right now that you're wrong.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What exactly are we? My answer is that the Chrysos Heirs are the future Titans, and vice versa. Of course, this answer only applies to us.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: So, what are "we" when it comes to regular mortals?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: The very essence of the world — our souls — are tiny invisible seeds that hold records of each person's memories of the world, and "we" are the buds that sprout from these seeds to grow into great trees.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Is that what Nousporism means?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Correct. Once our physical bodies are born, we become new extensions of the world. From there, we plant our seeds into someone's memories and then scatter them into the hearts of countless people in the future.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Just as seeds are affected by their environment, so too will our appearances differ across memories. But the partial memories we carry will always be the same, because that is just how the world is.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: To destroy our very existence, one must destroy the world itself. But we have someone who will still live on with his perfect memory...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: That person is you, child of Kephale. This is what it means to be the Worldbearing Titan.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: So, carry everything of this world and live on. Don't disappoint those most precious to you. Don't disappoint Lady Goldweaver.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: And especially don't bring dishonor to my theory.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Anaxa, I swear to you. I'll lead everyone to our reunion in the new world.
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Hmph, good.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: That's all I have to say. Farewell, everyone. May we meet again in the next life.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Farewell, Great Performer. May Cerces safeguard your thoughts.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Are you satisfied, honorable Titan?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Very. I hereby swear I have borne witness: Anaxagoras of the Nousporists and the Grove of Epiphany has successfully overcome the trial of Reason.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Thus, I shall confer upon you these words.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: "You shall transcend the peaks of purity and return to corruption and hardship."
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Oh, so that's a god's prophecy? It sounds like you just rephrased my past, present, and future.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh, Cerces, Cerces. Is that all you've got?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Well, you've already "transcended the peaks of purity" and you were never the type to give me any leeway.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: Hmph, that is true.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: But I do still have one question.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: I knew it...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: What is it? Maybe we're thinking of the same thing.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: As you've so boldly stated, we and the world itself live on through the memories of others.
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: If that is the case, whose memories did the very first nouspore sprout from?
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: How should I know?
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Oh my...
rows.speaker: Cerces

rows.text: But since we are both equally curious...
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: We should allow the children of humanity who come after us to investigate in our stead.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: ...Thankfully, she's still alive.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Was March 7th also in this condition when she was first rescued by the Express?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Her condition was very similar. It's just that at that time, the Express did not have a Memokeeper who could diagnose her condition.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: But she still woke up naturally. Looking on the bright side, that might happen this time as well.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: When March awakened from the ice, her memories were completely wiped clean. I want to prepare for the worst and prevent something like that from happening again.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Can you share with us your hypothesis?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I do not have conclusive evidence, but judging by her current condition...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Perhaps March 7th's memories have been hijacked.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Hijacked?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Think about it, Miss Himeko. What will happen when someone loses their ability to remember?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I'm not a biologist, but I hear that there's of a species of fish on Vonwacq that has the memory span of less than a second. It forgets anything that occurs in the very next instant. Perhaps something similar will happen?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Unfortunately, short-term memory is an entirely different concept from the inability to remember. Perhaps it is difficult for you to imagine...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: But an individual who has lost their ability to remember turns into nothingness.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Nothingness?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: The belief of the Garden is that everything in this universe can be interpreted through memories. This is the driving force behind the continuance of this Path.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: The past is made up of memoria while the future is a possibility that will eventually be converted to memoria. But the present... it doesn't really exist and is only an abstract expression.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Therefore, when a person is affected by the Path and loses their ability to remember... their physical form will also be affected. These ice crystals are a manifestation of that.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: ...Miss Black Swan, there is one thing that I haven't looked into deeply until now.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You've guided us to Amphoreus but refused to tell us your true intentions. "Collecting memories"... is simply not a convincing answer.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: Is Miss Himeko suspicious of me?
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I mean no offense. I am merely speculating. But I'd appreciate your honesty, if possible.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: In other words, now is the time for me to prove my innocence...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: That's not a problem, of course. The true reason behind my intentions is that Amphoreus holds special significance. For some Memokeepers of the Garden with extremist views, it... is a "perfect example."
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Perfect example?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: A world that can only be seen through the Garden's mirror means that Memokeepers have the right to keep the world in their private collection. If those pathstriders of Remembrance were to uncover the secrets of Amphoreus first...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: They might unleash their wild ambitions and remodel more worlds into a similar form.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: So, the reason you did everything you could to convince the Express to come to this star zone is just to uncover the secrets and foil the plans of these people?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I chose to remain quiet before because I did not want to involve you in the Garden's internal conflicts.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Remodeling a world is no easy feat. These extremists likely aren't just simple pathstriders. Do they wield the powers of Emanators?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: You can be even bolder with your guesses. The people that I'm talking about... They aren't just individuals. They are an organization that has already attached itself to the pinky finger of Fuli.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: So what you're saying... Could they be the ones who hijacked March 7th's memories?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I cannot be certain, but at the very least, they are capable of doing so.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: I am deeply sorry about what has happened to March 7th, but the deal that I proposed still remains a fair one. Amphoreus is still an excellent destination, and investigating further might allow us to uncover the truth behind the accident.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Miss Himeko, the wisest choice right now is for us to continue cooperating...
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: What's wrong?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: ...Let me take back a part of what I said just now, Miss Himeko.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Although we indeed struck a deal, it seems like I have involved you in some unforeseen danger... Please accept my deepest apologies.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: Has something changed?
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: It's Fuli... THEIR gaze has just swept across Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Black Swan

rows.text: But... I don't see Castorice among your number.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: It looks like she not only helped me prove my theory, but helped you fulfill your mission as well.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Trinnon, please recite the prophecy for us. [Trailblazer], please surrender that scalding Coreflame for us as well.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: You are the only life she ever saved by her own hand in her one thousand years on this earth. I believe no one is more qualified for this noble task.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: The Hand of Shadow, Thanatos, remembered their name from the past! From daylight they came and to their fragrant dwelling they return, to walk now among your ranks.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: And there was one who joined hands with the Titan. A traveler risen from the dead and reborn among mortal kind. {M#He}{F#She} is the everlasting night and shall now proclaim in {M#his}{F#her} good name:
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: "O majesty of the Twelve Titans, pillars of the world—"
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: "We seek your divinity, to mend the rifts of the world —"
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: "Fill our bodies with blood of gold, till we wither in willing service to the prophecy..."
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Step forward, Trailblazer from beyond the sky. And together with us...
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Surrender the Coreflame and carve their star into the sky.
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: A constellation for Death...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: For Life and Death, to be more precise.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: Look! It's...
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Is that... Castorice?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: No, it's only a Divine Echo. I think she's here for the trial.
rows.speaker: Anaxa

rows.text: *Titan's murmurs*
rows.speaker: Divine Echo

rows.text: What did she say?
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: That's the language of the Titans...
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: Castorice... No, the Titan...
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: They said...
rows.speaker: Trinnon

rows.text: "...I have illuminated the cold shadow of death."
rows.speaker: Divine Echo

rows.text: "Onwards. For your path to the future is bright and its flame eternal."
rows.speaker: Divine Echo

rows.text: "Do not forget..."
rows.speaker: Divine Echo

rows.text: First Mirror, input the coordinates. You'll be in charge of the spatial warp.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: As you command, Madam Herta.
rows.speaker: First Mirror

rows.text: The preparations are complete. I wish you a pleasant journey ahead.
rows.speaker: First Mirror

rows.text: Second Mirror, prepare for the Thought Refraction. There's still some distance from the Astral Express to the Amphoreus celestial body. You're in charge of sending me over...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: This time raise the power to the maximum. Don't be stingy!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: O—Okay, I won't fail the mission, Madam Herta...
rows.speaker: Second Mirror

rows.text: Third Mirror, you're in charge of generating the "data spirit entity."
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Hehehe... I'm happy to help, Madam Herta...
rows.speaker: Third Mirror

rows.text: Hehehe... What kind of appearance are you planning to use this time?
rows.speaker: Third Mirror

rows.text: Good question. Let me think...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Forget it. Just use my own appearance. There's no one there that'll recognize me anyway.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Hehehe, as you wish...
rows.speaker: Third Mirror

rows.text: Fourth Mirror, you'll be in charge of...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It seems like I have nothing for you. Just stand by and wait for orders.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Ah? Standing by again? That's so boring...
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Next time, can you count down from four instead...?
rows.speaker: Fourth Mirror

rows.text: Thank you, Madam Herta. Companions are the lifeblood of the Astral Express. When things are settled, we will repay you for all your help.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: (Welt... This young man sure is courteous.)
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Madam, watching you work has been an enlightening experience for me. It's hard to imagine that an outstanding scholar like you could maintain such a... relaxed manner most of the time.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Your calm and collected nature is truly a trait that I should learn.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: (This brat... Why does everything that comes out of his mouth sound so snarky?)
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Agh... I didn't expect it to be so turbulent. I should have asked the Second Mirror to use slightly less power.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh... What a magnificent sight. Is this the entrance to Amphoreus?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Let's see. Perhaps I'll be able to find a way in?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Oh, I've finally found your... traces.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: How esteemed must you be for the great Herta to come out personally! When we return, get ready to become free labor for the Simulated Universe for the rest of your lives.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What's this? How creepy.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...Oh, it moves? Who are you trying to scare?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It's either a projection or a fake. There doesn't seem to be much to take note of.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Now then... How am I going to get into Amphoreus?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Alright, now that everything is ready...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Mirrors, get to work.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...Oh? How interesting.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I never expected a mere Memosnatcher to be actually hiding so much inside her head.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: What's even more interesting is that the word "Amphoreus" has appeared in her subconscious.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: This lady... seems to be having fun. Is she usually like this?
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...It's hard to explain.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: What are you two whispering about? Has it not occurred to you that I can hear everything clearly?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Please pardon me, Madam Herta. Would you mind sharing with us what you've discovered?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Hmph, the ones who need help are the Astral Express. You will have to put up with my methods, even if they are rather unconventional.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Let's get back to the topic. By using the Fourth Mirror, I rummaged through the brain of this Memosnatcher and learned a good deal.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Not only does this person know of Amphoreus, but there are also many Memokeepers who are interested in the place.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I searched through her consciousness and found the following terms: "The Eternal Land," "The Rejected Land," and "the Private Collection of the Garden of Recollection"...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It seems like Miss Black Swan is indeed hiding some things from us.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Since I'm not able to find any useful clues from the outside, why don't I personally visit this mysterious Amphoreus?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: You're planning to head to Amphoreus yourself?
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Yes, but not in the flesh, like you all foolishly did.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: See these Herta Mirrors? With them, I can project my "data spirit entity" to any corner of the cosmos through spatial warps, without even needing to leave my room.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: But of course, these "corners of the cosmos" must be within the coverage zone of Interastral Peace Communications. After all, this is collaborative technology.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I see. You do seem like the more... "indoor" type.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: Although that star zone is not within the network of the IPC, the Express itself can serve as a signal station. Come, give me the astral chart coordinates.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Then, sit back and enjoy the show.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Welt shares the Astral Express's coordinates with The Herta...
Preparation of the data spirit entity, complete.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Thought Refraction, at max power.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Excellent — First Mirror, let's get going.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Have a safe trip, Madam Herta.
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: May your journey yield good results.
rows.speaker: Sunday

rows.text: ...Coordinates input complete. Preparing to activate spatial warp. Destination: Unknown celestial body, Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: First Mirror

rows.text: Spatial warp countdown: Five, four, three, two, one...
rows.speaker: First Mirror

rows.text: Warp activated.
rows.speaker: First Mirror

rows.text: Oh... So that's Amphoreus? Its appearance is — well — sure is unique.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Second Mirror, prepare for Thought Refraction — it's time to send me in!
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Alright, p—please read the safety protocols carefully...
rows.speaker: Second Mirror

rows.text: Can't you hurry up?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Y—Yes, ma'am!
rows.speaker: Second Mirror

rows.text: My deepest apologies, esteemed lady. I'm afraid that you cannot proceed further.
Who's there?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Your visit, although not part of my calculations, is a pleasant surprise. It's a pity that the preparations are not yet in place to receive you with the hospitality that someone of your status deserves.
Are you not going to answer my question? Who are you?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I have many identities, and I'm going to have even more in the future. But if you just need a form of address, you can use my common alias...
Lycurgus, Lygus.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Alright, Lygus. But you can't possibly think that I'm just asking for a name, can you?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Regrettably, I do not have the authority to share more information.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: However, standards are always flexible. While not violating the ultimate protocol, I'm able to disclose this piece of information: As you thought, this is the entrance to Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Now, please kindly turn back. Amphoreus is not a world that you should be involved with. Regardless of what kind of magnificent achievements you have accomplished, this place will not open its doors so easily.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You seem to understand me very well. Then you should know that I have no reason to listen to you.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Your reaction is completely within my calculations. Despite my long years as a watcher, it seems like my assessment of human nature still remains accurate. From you, I am able to sense a beautiful desire for knowledge.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: But my answer remains unchanged. Madam, it is with the utmost goodwill that I suggest you return to where you came from.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Let's assume for a second that I'm not so well-mannered and that I insist on uncovering the secrets hidden behind you, Mr. Lygus...
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: ...How do you plan to dispel this notion of mine?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Within the scope of the ultimate protocol, there are 178,244 logic chains at my disposal to convince you.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: After filtering through them, I have determined that I only require three to attain the results that I desire.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Oh? I'm all ears.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: First: For reasons that cannot be disclosed, Amphoreus is a completely isolated celestial body. Apart from me, no one else will be able to help you enter.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: That's not a good argument.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Second: If your plan is — as you've alluded to previously — to force me into cooperating by showing hostility, do know that...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Just like you, I have basked in the gaze of the Erudition. I stake my honor and assure you that in the worst-case scenario, our mutual destruction will be inevitable.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: No wonder I couldn't find a backdoor when I did a scan of our surroundings. The safety protocols on you... are comparable to Screwy's. How interesting.
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: I assume that you still wish to hear the third logic chain?
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Of course. Why wouldn't I?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: Third: Even if you exhaust all your means and find a way to break through...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You will surely give up once you understand the consequences of your actions. After all, throughout your long life — as much as you'd hate to admit — your conscience has played a crucial role.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: Haha! What a brazen robot. You think that you can actually understand me through your paltry calculations?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: But since you've put it that way, why don't you tell me what these consequences will be?
rows.speaker: Herta

rows.text: It concerns the third Path that is entangled with Amphoreus — a Path that you and your friends still very much lack understanding of...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: The Destruction. So, if you ignore my warnings and persist in your ways...
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: You will break the shackles of a Lord Ravager, and when that happens, their fury will engulf the cosmos.
rows.speaker: Lygus

rows.text: This is Castorice's gift...?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: H—Holy Maiden...
rows.speaker: Courageous Warrior

rows.text: Go. Grant her glorious death.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: Do it then! Executioner...
rows.speaker: Outlander War Captive

rows.text: You heard him.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: Please... grant me release...
rows.speaker: Ill Herder

rows.text: You know what to do.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: Come. Fulfill your duty.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: ...What?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Come now. It's time. I have already taught you all that I know...
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: Show me that you are a fitting Holy Maiden... or at least, that you possess the resolve to become one.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: A gentle touch.
No... No...
rows.speaker: Unknown Death-Row Prisoner
