rows.text: No. I can't do it.
This is your duty. Remember, consider the source of the dead's suffering, then give them the respect they deserve.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: A gentle touch.
I—I can't...
If you cannot learn to accept death, then Aidonia has no place for you.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: A gentle touch.
I... I can't do it.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Their voices... They pierce my ears... The pleading, the thanks...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Ahh. I know that feeling, child. I was once as lost as you are now.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: But you must respect those walking towards death, just like how you should respect yourself as the Holy Maiden granting humans glory and liberation.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: What you're asking me to do is no better than the task of an executioner, and yet you want me to respect myself?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: No matter the titles, I am still taking away human lives...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This won't be the first time that Aidonia's fanatical netherwarriors have faced death. On the contrary, recruits new to the battlefield often run away from their first fight.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: Death is the mightiest and gravest power in this world. The fact that you can wield it means you are deserving of respect.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: That's such a... twisted reason...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Then, let me tell you a story.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: In Aidonia, the greatswords commonly used by executioners are called "Drakonian" in memory of Drakon, an elderly executioner.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: The sword has three air holes along its body. If the sword is swung down swiftly and accurately, the holes would make no sound, and the executed would also depart this world quickly and painlessly...
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: But should the executioner have any hesitation, the holes will produce a piercing whistle. On that cue, the screams of the executed are sure to follow.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: Every executioner after Drakon is to hone their sword skills every day in preparation of future executions. Every swing of their blade must be more resolute than the last, for failing to do so will bring pain.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: Pain for the dying... as well as pain for themselves.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: ...No. I can never get used to this.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You misunderstand, child. I am not telling you to get used to it.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: I'm asking you to consider the source of the dead's suffering, and use that knowledge to fortify your future touches with more and more determination.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: Go walk with the dead, and love them as you love life... Then you'll no longer hear those noises.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: ...What are you trying to do with me?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I have aged... The time has come for me to heed the summons of {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} and journey to their domain.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: ...The final resting place of every Aidonian.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: You're not that old yet... You still have many, many years ahead of you...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: No no... I'm already "dead."
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: For I have come to fear... my declining health and impending death.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: Castorice, will you give me one last chance to charge towards fear and prove that I am no coward?
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: I... I can't take this anymore...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Child, it was I who brought you here from the frosty plains and set your farcical fate in motion. It was also I, chief executioner of Aidonia, who forced the heavy duty of executing others onto you.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: I've always known... that you have doubts and even anger about {RUBY_B#Aidonian}my{RUBY_E#} faith... and about me...
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: I... never had a choice...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Indeed. We essentially abducted you.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: Yet you can end any sinful life with just a touch of your fingers... Shouldn't it be easy for you escape from here?
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: ...I'll never do that.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It doesn't matter how lightly the Aidonians take death, or how readily they accept it... I simply can't do it.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Haha... I knew I was right about you.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: Wh—What do you mean?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I've taught you and cared for you as my own daughter all this time... because of this {RUBY_B#curse}blessing{RUBY_E#} that's been with you since your birth. I know no one else in the world would understand the weight of life and death more than you do.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: In the eyes of an Aidonian, "Death" is the end of all life, a destination we will all eventually reach. Humans should not resist it, but learn how to face it.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: You can only live your life to the fullest after understanding this principle.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: And when you do, even if you eventually leave Aidonia's protection... even if you must carry the {RUBY_B#blessing}curse{RUBY_E#} forever... you can live with your head held high, like everyone else.
rows.speaker: "Elder" Amunet

rows.text: No, how can I—
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: This was the last time I followed her command. I gently touched the elderly woman before me.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The executioner who had seen too much death died the same way as everyone else... A gasp for air, a wistful look in her eyes, and a barely perceptible tremor in her fingertips.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Elder Amunet, the person who tried to teach me about "Death," ultimately vanished like dew in the morning mist. She spent her life embodying the beliefs of the Aidonians, and when death finally came, she embraced it exactly as their doctrine had taught...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I have nothing but respect for her.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I erected a cenotaph in her honor in the marshes outside Aidonia's city walls with the others I had laid to rest. Then, I set out once more in search of {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It was a long, long journey... I heard so many discussions about death along the way. "Life finds meaning in death." "The world improves because there is an end"...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: It seems the most terrible darkness in this world. Everyone talks about its heavy weight. Some resist it, some worship it, and some even revere it...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: How did a disappeared Titan become the deepest fear of humankind...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...And why do they haunt my dreams?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I continued my travels to seek an answer. Initially, I was running away. Then, I started searching for it. And now, at the end...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I just want to know if my touch... if my embrace... can do more than taking things away...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Can I make anything...? Can I leave anything behind?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: On the day that {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx's{RUBY_E#} Trial ended, you must have had many questions, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I felt just as confused. Why, as someone from beyond the sky, were you so cruelly dragged into Amphoreus's fate?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...I wished I could take action, but no matter how hard I try, I cannot simply interact with the living as ordinary people do.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Even when we brushed against each other unintentionally in the Grove... and it was obvious that nothing had happened...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: When an almost unattainable hope finally welled up in my heart...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: When I thought that perhaps my touch would no longer bring sorrow...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Fate declared to me: It wasn't that the curse of "Death" had finally been lifted...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...but that your soul no longer belonged to this world... and there was nothing left for my hands to take. Nothing.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: And did I really think this time would be any different? It's not that I don't understand this reality — just that I'm unwilling to accept it.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Having walked such a long road, I am still unable to find the answer to life and death. I am resigned to eternal despair...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Anything I wish to hold on to, "Death" will inevitably wrest from my grasp...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: And from that moment on, I lacked the courage to confirm it again... Until {RUBY_B#Time Titan}Oronyx{RUBY_E#} laid bare the cruel truth before us.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Then, what was left of my reason was left behind in the nether realm...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Where I've been taking care of these flowers day after day, until there is now a sea of them....
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: ...All while mulling over the subject of life, death, partings, and enduring an endless loneliness.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: I had a feeling even back then that we would meet again one day...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Not to embrace one another after a long separation, but to come in search of retribution.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Tell me the answer that's already been written... and let us draw this seemingly endless fate to a close.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: ...Fate is absurd indeed.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Our lives were a mirrored image of one another, like a pair of hands... Even so, we arrived at the same destination.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: We walked different paths, yet experienced the same pain.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I had hoped that maybe you would at least have a good life in this cycle...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: ...I'm sorry.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: I lived my life well. It didn't go to waste. As far as I'm concerned, you did nothing wrong.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Even though I forced the authority of "granting death to humanity" upon you, a total stranger?
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Too many responsibilities were forced upon me in the course of this long journey. I was once lost, even upset...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But I realized recently that if it weren't for your blessing, I wouldn't have understood the source of these emotions, nor would I have realized my purpose...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I wouldn't have made it here to reunite with my missing half, and we wouldn't be discussing our past while sharing the same view of this landscape...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I wouldn't have understood the meaning of our "existence."
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The meaning of our existence...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: This sea of flowers blooms on dead land because we sowed it with the seeds of our separation and watered it with our tears of loneliness... Yes, the only thing "Death" is allowed to create are flowers that bloom from blood and tears.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That's why {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} cannot create living beings at will, nor can the {RUBY_B#Death Titan}"Hand of Shadow"{RUBY_E#} determine a person's remaining days...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Because the life and death of mortals should never be dictated by another's will.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Are you saying there's no point in {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}' existence...?
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: No. No single being can bear the scales of life and death on their own, not even a god.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Life and death weigh equally heavy... We both know that now, don't we?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You, too, must have had a difficult life...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: We've taken quite the ridiculous journey together, haven't we?
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: It's been far too long. I've waited here for centuries, watching day after day as desperate spirits are denied by this lonely wasteland...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: I always hoped I would see you among them, but I was also afraid of seeing you. I didn't know how I could possibly face you again...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: But... more than anything, I was afraid that you might have forgotten all about me.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: ...I know. But don't you see, Polyxia? I made it back anyway.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You don't have to shoulder Death's authority on your own anymore... It was always meant to be held in two hands anyway.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: So, let's give our Coreflame to [Trailblazer] and have {M#him}{F#her} take it back to the mortal realm. Give humanity back their cycle of life and death.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Our responsibility as {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} was never about picking out favorite souls. We were only meant to watch over life.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Let's tend the field together and create a warm sea of flowers for all the souls to come.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: What do you think, Polyxia?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yes. Just... one last step.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: "You shall wither, and through that, the dead will sprout again from the remains, and be reborn with the dead flame"...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: As foretold by the prophecy, Thanatos' authority is only destined for only one person to wield. As the Chrysos Heir of "Death," as their demigod, as a Titan...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: ...Our fated moment has arrived once again.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Just like before...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yes, just like before.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: But unlike that time, the ones undergoing the trial this time are prepared.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: You've... made up your mind?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yes... as dictated by fate. But I won't be afraid, as long as you're here with me.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Complete your trial in this life. Grant me the embrace of "Death" and light the spark of "Life" ablaze.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: You've been tempered by life and death. I know you'll be able to give this wasteland its first breath of life...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Like a raven butterfly flying swiftly into the nether realm, perching on the twig of death.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: ...I will. After this, I will remain permanently in the nether realm. The River of Souls shall return here and rain down from the sky, scattering souls across the earth...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: The cycle of life and death will flow once again. This sea of flowers you sowed shall bear countless joyous or sorrowful souls, and bloom evermore.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Thank you.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Just one last thing. Can you... grant me one wish?
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Of course. What is it?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please... don't forget me.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: ...I promise you.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: When we meet in the next world... Even if I have endured another reincarnation...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...Even if we do not know each other's names...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...I will still hold you tightly in my arms, just like what I did when we were born.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Castorice... Castorice...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: You're as beautiful... as a fleeting butterfly.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text:
Oh, you sit in your little dinghy
Eager to hear my song and follow closely behind
Please, turn back, return to the homeland you know so well

Venture not with me into the vast sea, for perhaps
Without seeing me, you will lose your way in the ocean
The ocean I cross has never been sailed by anyone
After all that...
You still ended up back here.
So the legends were true. The nether realm really is a sea of flowers.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yes.
Just like the flower fields we tended to back then...
Is that you... Polyxia?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Do you remember me?
...I don't have the memories from that time, but I've seen you before during an experiment.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I see.
Call me {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} then. It'll be easier.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: However, since you recognize the name, you must already know everything about {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}, right?
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Yes....
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: I'm... here to reforge the order of life and death in Amphoreus.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You know, my sister was a sympathetic but rather sensitive person. Whenever she didn't want to say what was on her mind, she would avoid eye contact and look off into the distance...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Just like what you are doing now.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Can you tell me... about the last Era Nova?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: What did you do, Polyxia?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Where should I begin...? I suppose we can start from the beginning.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: A long, long time ago, there were a pair of like-minded twins. As foretold in the prophecy, they were chosen to be successors to the god of "Death."
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: But fate was cruel. The price of attaining divinity was to take the life of our closest kin with our own hands.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: That trial... was indeed recorded in that memory.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Then you should already know that my sister voluntarily gave up her own life so that I could ascend as the demigod of "Death."
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: But I couldn't accept that. Why did we have to kill each other for a future she'd never see herself? That's not fair.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: So, while weaving the laws of the new world... I shattered the forbidden bottom line for "life" and "death."
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: I reshaped my sister's soul and took the form of the great dragon Pollux to carry her up the River of Souls and back into the mortal realm.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: But our fates were already decided... and manifested in unexpected ways in response to my futile actions.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Aging is an unbreakable law of nature laid upon humankind, created at the same time as "Death." When the living die, their souls will meet {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}, who would determine where every soul goes...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: If the Reaper raises their left hand, the soul is granted death and allowed to enter the nether realm to await reincarnation. If they raise their right hand, the soul is rejected by the nether realm and returned to the mortal realm to continue walking the earth.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: That's why the {RUBY_B#Death Titan}"Hand of Shadow"{RUBY_E#} can only lay down judgment... and not embrace another being.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yes. "Death" was originally a pair of hands, but they were split in twain when we reached the mortal realm, never to touch each other ever again...
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: The half of {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#} that represents life, the undying human who "grants death"... That was the curse I forced upon you.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: Then... What about you?
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: As the half of Thanatos representing death, I shoulder the fate of "defying death." I died the moment I entered the world of the living.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: From then on, my Titan also no longer existed in this world. The cycle of life and death stopped. Souls were denied their audience with death, and were left stranded within an ever-rising river of the dead....
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: What irony. My selfish desire to save your life gave you and the world a fate far worse than death instead.
rows.speaker: Thanatos

rows.text: [Trailblazer], don't look back.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Life and death are predetermined, but yours life doesn't end here.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Listen, your home is not there.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: Look for the direction of the falling stars when you're lost.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Little Gray, you won't find tomorrow there!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: Don't look back. Don't make Castorice regret this.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Only the weak will be hindered by the far-reaching grasp of Calamity. Are you one of them?
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Partner, don't you dare lose to the shadows of death!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: Please, I beg you, look back for me.
rows.speaker: Calls of the Dead

rows.text: Death is such a sweet joy...
rows.speaker: Calls of the Dead

rows.text: A warm embrace awaits you...
rows.speaker: Calls of the Dead

rows.text: Just forget about all the hardships of the mortal realm.
rows.speaker: Calls of the Dead

rows.text: Don't go.
rows.speaker: Calls of the Dead

rows.text: [Trailblazer], over here!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Keep moving forward and don't look back.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Keep going. The Express is right here with you.
rows.speaker: Himeko

rows.text: I believe in you, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Welt

rows.text: Listen: just keep moving.
rows.speaker: Kafka

rows.text: One day, our paths will cross again.
rows.speaker: Firefly

rows.text: Lift your chin up high and step forward with us toward tomorrow!
rows.speaker: Trianne

rows.text: That's right. Keep your eyes on the dawn.
rows.speaker: Aglaea

rows.text: Onward! Show me your courage.
rows.speaker: Mydei

rows.text: Partner, we shall become heroes together!
rows.speaker: Phainon

rows.text: (Almost there...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: It's a beautiful place.
Every departed soul who has arrived here has expressed the same.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Mom, I made it! My character arc is finally done!
You're still as energetic as always.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Did you know? Every flower here was planted by Thanatos themself. These flowers were originally both lifeless and immortal, but in the first rain brought by the River of Souls, they were given new life, flourishing as the bearers of countless souls...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You have my word.
Thank you.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: You're... not going back?
Mm, just like the other demigods, I will stay here... and embrace my destiny.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But at what cost?

Rest assured, "defying death" is {RUBY_B#Death Titan}Thanatos{RUBY_E#}' divine authority. Fortunately, your soul hasn't dissipated. This is not a resurrection, but the extradition of a dying person back to the present world.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: But you're not going back...
So you're not going back...
I'll do my best.
I am... glad to hear that.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Don't turn around. Keep looking forward.
(What's this...!?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Don't turn around. Keep looking forward.
Don't turn around. Keep looking forward.
Don't turn around. Keep looking forward.
Don't turn around. Keep looking forward.
Goodbye, nether realm.
...Let the Trailblazing... continue.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hello again, mortal realm.
(A sea of flowers...?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (What... is this place?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Allow me to reintroduce myself: I bore the name of Castorice while walking among the mortals, and now I stand as the demigod of Death, the living side of Thanatos...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Welcome to my realm, where the west wind ends.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: And it is my duty as the master of Death to tend to their well-being and foster their growth in this serene haven.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Similar to the structured cycle of life and death in the mortal world, these flowers too shall wither and fade, returning to the earth and then ascending to the sky with mist and tides...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Eventually, they will descend to the mortal land as gentle rain. Every soul undergoes the perpetual cycle of reincarnation, albeit in varied forms, until the world meets its end...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Yet, sadly, there's no time left for Amphoreus to wait for when the flowers bloom again.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Now, Death is the power at my fingertips. It once led the souls of the deceased here, but I... I shall open the gate of the netherworld and return you to the realm of the living...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: In exchange... Please, take the Coreflame of Death with you and complete the Flame-Chase Journey. Do not let our work thus far be in vain.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: That being said, it is not easy to guide a lost soul back to the mortal realm. The whispers of Death are sweet and alluring. If your determination wavers, you will succumb and be forever ensnared by the netherworld's grasp.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: Please consider this a one-time exception. I will do everything in my power for the Flame-Chase Journey...
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: ...And for your life, the only life I can save.
rows.speaker: Castorice

rows.text: (Finally...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (...Thank you, Castorice.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (Since I've already made it to the end, maybe I can have one last glance at that sea of flowers...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Fear not, as a touch of red will be awaiting you at the end of the path.
It'll guide you and illuminate the way out. By doing so... you'll eventually reunite in the warmth of the sunlight.
(What in the world are these shadows and voices...?)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: "All of this is proof that you once lived."
"Your soul, your memories, the years you've journeyed through, and the path {RUBY_B#Time Titan, Oronyx}they{RUBY_E#} revealed, leading you back home."
"So, continue onward. Do not stop moving forward, and do not let her sacrifice and the support of all who have stood by you be in vain..."
Over here, friend...!
rows.speaker: Mem

rows.text: Take my hand. Let's go home...!
rows.speaker: Mem
